title: OCIRegistry CRD accepts keyless config the API rejects
description:
internal/api/registry.go:validateVerificationConfig returns 400 when verificationMode is 'keyless' without both trustIdentity and trustIssuer. The CRD has no equivalent constraint: api/v1alpha1/ociregistry_types.go:64-82 marks VerificationMode with an Enum and default, but TrustPublicKey, TrustIdentity and TrustIssuer are all bare +optional with no cross-field rule.

An operator-managed OCIRegistry can therefore be admitted with mode=keyless and no identity/issuer — a configuration the HTTP API considers invalid. Same for mode=public_key with no trustPublicKey.

Add +kubebuilder:validation:XValidation CEL rules to the spec so both paths enforce the same invariant, then 'make generate-operator' and commit the regenerated CRDs.
acceptance_criteria: A CEL rule rejects keyless without identity+issuer and public_key without a key at admission time. config/operator/crd/*.yaml is regenerated. The API and CRD enforce identical invariants.
notes:
Files: internal/api/registry.go, internal/api/registry_test.go, api/v1alpha1/ociregistry_types.go, config/operator/crd/ocidex.io_ociregistries.yaml
Approach: validateVerificationConfig now also rejects public_key mode without trust_public_key (previously unenforced by the API at all — TestValidateVerificationConfig_OtherModesUnaffected asserted this as a no-op). Added matching struct-level +kubebuilder:validation:XValidation CEL rules on OCIRegistrySpec for both keyless and public_key, using size(x) > 0 instead of != '' to sidestep a tool-layer smart-quote corruption issue hit while editing. Regenerated CRD via make generate-operator. Unit tests pass, make lint clean (no new findings). Skipped live admission-time verification per user choice: only reachable cluster is the live Flux-managed homelab rpi-cluster, and its ociregistries.ocidex.io CRD is sourced from charts/ocidex-operator/crds/, which is discovered to be stale (missing verificationMode/trust* fields entirely, and untouched by make generate-operator) -- worth a separate follow-up issue.

title: reverifier: hardcoded ticker, no first tick, no enable flag, undocumented config
description:
internal/enrichment/reverify.go Run() has several rough edges:

- 'time.NewTicker(time.Hour)' is hardcoded, ignoring r.interval — which IS used for the recheck cutoff ('Cutoff: time.Now().Add(-r.interval)'). Interval and tick rate are silently decoupled.
- No immediate first tick: the sweep waits a full hour after startup before doing anything, so a short-lived pod never reverifies.
- No enable/disable flag. The reverifier runs unconditionally wherever it is wired up.
- PROVENANCE_RECHECK_INTERVAL appears in neither docs/CONFIGURATION.md nor .env.example.

Fix: derive the ticker from the configured interval, tick once immediately on start, add an explicit enable flag, and document the config.
acceptance_criteria: Ticker period derives from the configured interval. A sweep runs at startup. The reverifier can be disabled by configuration. PROVENANCE_RECHECK_INTERVAL and the enable flag are documented in docs/CONFIGURATION.md and .env.example.
notes:
Files: internal/enrichment/reverify.go, cmd/ocidex/main.go, internal/config/config.go, docs/CONFIGURATION.md, .env.example, internal/enrichment/reverify_test.go
Approach: Run() now builds the ticker from r.interval instead of a hardcoded hour, and ticks once immediately before entering the select loop. Added PROVENANCE_REVERIFIER_ENABLED config flag (default true, preserving current unconditional behavior) gating the main.go LeaderElect wiring, mirroring the ScannerEnabled/RegistryPollerEnabled pattern. Documented both PROVENANCE_RECHECK_INTERVAL and the new flag in docs/CONFIGURATION.md and .env.example. Added TestReverifier_Run_TicksImmediatelyOnStart and TestReverifier_Run_TicksAtConfiguredInterval covering Run() (previously only tick() was tested).

title: TUF trusted-root fetch serialises workers under mutex and staleness is unbounded
description:
getTrustedRoot() in internal/enrichment/provenance/keyless.go holds the cache mutex for the entire duration of root.FetchTrustedRoot(), an unbounded network round trip with no context. Every concurrent enrichment worker therefore serialises behind one TUF fetch.

Second issue in the same function: the stale-serve fallback has no bound. If TUF keeps failing, the cached root is served indefinitely, which means revoked Fulcio CAs remain trusted forever — a fail-open with no ceiling.

Fix: fetch outside the lock (single-flight, e.g. golang.org/x/sync/singleflight, already a likely indirect dep), pass a context with timeout, and refuse to serve a root older than some hard maximum (a multiple of trustedRootCacheTTL) rather than serving it forever.
acceptance_criteria: Concurrent verifications do not serialise behind the TUF fetch. The fetch honours a context deadline. A trusted root older than the configured hard maximum causes verification to fail rather than proceed on stale trust material.
notes:
Files: internal/enrichment/provenance/keyless.go, internal/enrichment/provenance/keyless_test.go
Approach: getTrustedRoot no longer holds trustedRootMu across the TUF fetch. Concurrent
callers on a stale/empty cache now collapse into one in-flight fetch via
golang.org/x/sync/singleflight (already a direct dep; errgroup from the same module is
used in internal/service/search_stats.go). The fetch is bounded by a 30s context timeout
via tuf.Options.WithContext (root.FetchTrustedRoot itself takes no context). The stale-serve
fallback on fetch error now has a hard ceiling, trustedRootMaxStaleness = 7 * trustedRootCacheTTL
(7 days) -- beyond that, verification fails closed instead of trusting indefinitely-stale
material. Added fetchTrustedRootFn test seam (mirrors existing trustedMaterialProvider
pattern) and 5 new tests covering cache-hit-skips-fetch, singleflight collapse, context
deadline propagation, stale-served-within-ceiling, and fail-closed-beyond-ceiling. Verified
with go test -race on the provenance package and golangci-lint (only pre-existing,
unrelated findings remain, e.g. the unparam finding tracked separately as ocidex-goh.17).
Full-repo make check/make test could not be run in this session due to the host disk
being nearly full (unrelated to this change) -- flagged to the user.

title: provenance drift banner never clears after recovery
description:
lookupProvenanceDrift (internal/service/search_sbom.go:137) returns GetLatestProvenanceDrift unconditionally, and ProvenanceCard.tsx renders it under <Show when={drift}>. Because drift recording is regression-only (recordProvenanceDrift returns early unless the old status was 'verified' or 'signed'), recovery is never recorded.

Result: once an artifact is removed and later restored, the SBOM detail page shows a green 'Verified' badge directly above the text 'changed from verified to artifact_missing on <date>' — permanently, and self-contradictorily.

Two viable fixes: (a) only surface the drift summary when drift.NewStatus still equals the current detail.SigningStatus; or (b) record recovery transitions as drift events too and let the banner describe the latest transition either way. (b) is more informative and makes the drift feed a complete history rather than a regression log.
acceptance_criteria: A recovered SBOM does not display a stale drift banner contradicting its current signing status. Behaviour is covered by a test.
notes:
Files: internal/service/search_sbom.go, internal/service/search_test.go
Approach: gate SBOMDetail.ProvenanceDrift on drift.NewStatus == current signing status via new currentDrift() helper. Recovery is not itself recorded as a drift event, so once status changes away from a regression's NewStatus, the stale event is suppressed instead of shown forever.

title: refactor: single source of truth for signing status derivation
description:
The mapping from a provenance enrichment's JSON to a terminal signing status (unsigned | signed | verified | verification_failed | artifact_missing) is implemented five times across three languages:

  1-3. db/queries/artifact.sql — the CASE expression, duplicated 3x (ListArtifacts, GetArtifact, ListArtifactVersions)
  4.   internal/enrichment/provenance_drift.go:signingStatus()
  5.   web/src/utils/trust.ts:trustStatus()

Adding artifact_missing in ocidex-atd.13 required editing all five. A sixth status will too. The frontend copy is the weakest: it re-derives status from the raw provenance JSON blob rather than reading a server-computed value, so it can silently disagree with what the API sorts and filters on.
design:
Two moves:

DB side — collapse the three CASE copies into one Postgres function:
  CREATE FUNCTION signing_status(provenance_data jsonb) RETURNS text IMMUTABLE
and call it from all three queries in db/queries/artifact.sql. New migration; sqlc regenerates unchanged types since the return is still text.

API side — surface signingStatus as a first-class field on the SBOM/provenance response (it already exists on ArtifactVersionSummary). web/src/utils/trust.ts then maps status -> label/variant only, and stops inspecting p.verified / p.signaturePresent / p.artifactMissing.

internal/enrichment/provenance_drift.go:signingStatus() stays in Go — it must classify from two in-memory JSON blobs (old vs new) before either is queryable. But it should be the ONLY Go copy, and its doc comment should point at the SQL function as the normative definition. Consider a shared test fixture (table of provenance JSON -> expected status) asserted against both the Go function and the SQL function so they cannot drift apart silently.
acceptance_criteria: db/queries/artifact.sql contains one signing-status derivation, not three. web/src/utils/trust.ts consumes a server-provided status string and no longer re-derives from raw provenance fields. A parity test asserts the Go signingStatus() and the SQL function agree on a shared fixture table covering all five statuses. Adding a sixth status requires editing at most two places (SQL function + Go classifier).
notes:
Files: db/migrations/00049_signing_status_function.sql, db/queries/artifact.sql, internal/enrichment/provenance/status.go, internal/enrichment/provenance_drift.go, internal/service/search.go, internal/service/search_sbom.go, web/src/utils/trust.ts, web/src/components/ProvenanceCard.tsx, web/src/components/SummaryBand.tsx, web/src/pages/SBOMDetail/index.tsx, tests/integration_test.go
Approach: Consolidated 6 duplicate signing-status derivations into 3: signing_status(jsonb) Postgres function (used by GetArtifact/ListArtifacts/ListArtifactVersions), provenance.SigningStatus Go classifier (leaf package, avoids import cycle; replaces provenance_drift.go's local copy; also called from search_sbom.go to populate SBOMDetail.SigningStatus), and trust.ts's status->label/variant map (frontend now consumes server value via signingStatus prop instead of re-deriving from raw Provenance fields). Added TestSigningStatusParity_AllStatuses covering all 5 statuses (unsigned/signed/verified/verification_failed/artifact_missing), asserting Go classifier + SBOM detail endpoint + artifact detail endpoint all agree. Verified: make openapi, make frontend-lint (0 errors), go vet + targeted go test on service/enrichment/api packages (pass), golangci-lint scoped to changed packages (0 new issues vs pre-existing 53-issue baseline). Integration test compiles and skips cleanly without Docker in this environment (make test-integration not run — Docker unavailable).

title: refactor: unify public_key verification onto cosign.CheckOpts
description:
internal/enrichment/provenance/verify.go is ~120 lines of hand-rolled ECDSA + DSSE PAE crypto for the public_key verification path, while the keyless path (keyless.go, shipped in ocidex-atd.15) delegates to cosign/v2's own verify pipeline.

Two verification pipelines exist: one hardened by the reference implementation, one hand-written. The hand-written path re-implements digest binding itself (sigBoundDigest, subjectsBindTo) instead of reusing cosign's SimpleClaimVerifier / IntotoSubjectClaimVerifier, and silently accepts only ECDSA keys (parsePEMPublicKey type-asserts to *ecdsa.PublicKey).

cosign/v2 is already a direct dependency, so this costs zero new modules.
design:
Replace applyVerification's bespoke crypto with the same cosign.CheckOpts path applyKeylessVerification already uses, swapping TrustedMaterial/Identities for SigVerifier:

  verifier, err := signature.LoadVerifier(pubkey, crypto.SHA256)  // sigstore/sigstore/pkg/signature
  co := cosign.CheckOpts{SigVerifier: verifier, IgnoreTlog: true, IgnoreSCT: true}

Then reuse the existing buildOCISignature / buildStaticOptions helpers from keyless.go and call cosign.VerifyImageSignature / VerifyImageAttestation with ClaimVerifier set — identical structure to verifyKeylessSignature/verifyKeylessAttestation.

Note IgnoreTlog: true is correct here — a public-key signature has no Rekor bundle to check offline; that is the semantic difference from the keyless path, not an accident.

Deletes: parsePEMPublicKey, verifySig, verifyDSSE, sigBoundDigest, subjectsBindTo, dsseEnvelope (~100 lines).
Gains: RSA/ed25519 key support, shared claim verification, one crypto path to reason about.

Extract the shared setup (buildOCISignature, buildStaticOptions, the verify-sig-and-att AND-ing) so both modes call one helper differing only in CheckOpts construction.
acceptance_criteria: verify.go's hand-rolled ECDSA/DSSE crypto is deleted. Both public_key and keyless verification flow through cosign.VerifyImageSignature/VerifyImageAttestation with a ClaimVerifier set. Existing provenance_test.go public-key tests pass unchanged (they are the regression net). A test proves a public-key signature transplanted from a different image digest fails, mirroring TestApplyKeylessVerification_TransplantedSignatureFails. go.mod gains no new modules.
notes:
Files: internal/enrichment/provenance/{verify,keyless,parse,provenance,provenance_test}.go, go.mod
Approach: Rewrote applyVerification to build cosign.CheckOpts{SigVerifier: signature.LoadVerifier(cryptoutils.UnmarshalPEMToPublicKey(pemKey))} instead of hand-rolled ECDSA+DSSE-PAE crypto. Renamed verifyKeylessSignature/verifyKeylessAttestation -> verifyOCISignature/verifyOCIAttestation in keyless.go (now shared by both keyless and public_key paths, co determines trust source). Deleted subjectsBindTo/parsePEMPublicKey/verifySig/verifyDSSE from verify.go, and the now-orphaned simpleSigning/sigBoundDigest from parse.go (caught by golangci-lint unused, not by initial plan). go.mod: sigstore/sigstore promoted indirect->direct via go mod tidy, no version bump. Verified zero net-new lint findings via before/after full-repo golangci-lint diff (only delta was 2 pre-existing staticcheck hits in untouched internal/controller/ test files, confirmed reproducible independent of this change). Full test suite green.

title: Tekton Chains PipelineRun-level signing fails (signed=failed after 3 retries)
description: On push run ocidex-ocidex-push-l6bh5, the build TaskRun signed successfully (chains.tekton.dev/signed=true, image sig+attestation attached, Rekor logIndex 2247152855) but the PipelineRun-level annotation is chains.tekton.dev/signed=failed after chains.tekton.dev/retries=3. Per-image signing (TaskRun-level, drives signing_status) works; the aggregate PipelineRun SLSA provenance is not being stored. Investigate tekton-chains-controller logs for the PipelineRun deep-inspection signing/storage error (likely OCI push or subject-resolution for the pipeline-level attestation). Found while validating ocidex-07x.
notes:
RESOLVED in homelab, not ocidex. Fix: homelab-374 (commit fda1edc, pushed + Flux-reconciled).

Root cause: chains-config had artifacts.pipelinerun.storage: 'tekton, oci' (homelab talos-cluster/flux/apps/tekton-chains/kustomization.yaml:22). The 'tekton' backend writes the signed DSSE payload back as a k8s annotation; with enable-deep-inspection and ocidex's 10 image subjects the aggregate slsa/v2alpha4 payload exceeds the 262144-byte annotation limit:
  PipelineRun.tekton.dev "ocidex-ocidex-push-lzrqc" is invalid: metadata.annotations: Too long
  (chains/signing.go:265, tekton/tekton.go:76)
apko-cicd runs were signed=true because their payload stays under the limit.

The original report overstated the impact: the aggregate provenance was NEVER lost. For lzrqc the payload was signed, uploaded to Rekor, and the OCI backend pushed the attestation to all 10 images. Only the redundant annotation copy 422'd. The real cost was the retry storm - the reconciler re-ran the whole sign+store cycle each requeue, producing 9 Rekor entries and 90 OCI uploads per push run, plus a signed=failed status that misrepresented reality.

Fix: artifacts.pipelinerun.storage: 'oci'. TaskRun storage unchanged. No ocidex code touched - internal/enrichment/provenance/parse.go:91 reads chains.tekton.dev/transparency from the OCI manifest annotations, not the k8s object, so nothing here depended on the tekton backend.

Verified on a live re-sign of lzrqc: signed=true, 1 Rekor upload, 10 OCI uploads, 0 errors, cosign verify-attestation passes.
close_reason: Fixed in homelab-374 (Tekton Chains config); no ocidex code change required

title: Fix creds-init permission-denied on /.docker (pod-level runAsUser 1024 + no HOME)
description: Tekton's auto-injected creds-init container fails with 'mkdir /.docker: permission denied' across many CI jobs. Root cause: .tektonic/pipeline.ts's defaultPodSecurityContext (runAsUser: 1024) applies pod-wide via taskRunTemplate.podTemplate.securityContext, forcing creds-init (which materializes the ghcr-docker-config secret attached to the default ServiceAccount) to run as uid 1024. That uid has no /etc/passwd entry, so $HOME defaults to / (unwritable) -- same root cause class as the already-fixed GOPATH bug, but creds-init isn't a Task step so stepTemplate.env doesn't reach it.
design: Add { name: "HOME", value: "/tekton/home" } to podTemplateEnv in .tektonic/pipeline.ts. podTemplateEnv flows into taskRunTemplate.podTemplate.env, which per Tekton's own API schema applies to all containers in the pod (not just step containers), so it reaches creds-init. /tekton/home is already proven writable regardless of uid in this cluster (go-security.k8s.yaml steps already write there). No tektonic library change needed -- PACProject/TektonProject already plumb podTemplateEnv straight through to the real Tekton API field.
acceptance_criteria: Regenerated .tekton/*.k8s.yaml via make tekton-synth shows HOME=/tekton/home in the PipelineRun podTemplate.env. Verified live via an isolated TaskRun/PipelineRun that creds-init no longer logs the permission-denied warning.
notes:
Files: .tektonic/pipeline.ts, .tekton/ocidex-ocidex-{pull-request,push,tag}.k8s.yaml
Approach: defaultPodSecurityContext (runAsUser: 1024) applies pod-wide via taskRunTemplate.podTemplate.securityContext, including to Tekton's auto-injected creds-init step run by the entrypoint wrapper on every step. uid 1024 has no /etc/passwd entry so HOME defaults to '/', which is unwritable, causing 'mkdir /.docker: permission denied'. Added HOME=/tekton/home to podTemplateEnv (also pod-wide per Tekton's PodTemplate API), same writable-scratch pattern already used for stepTemplate.env (goEnv/nodeEnv). No tektonic library change needed - confirmed via pac-project.ts and the v1 swagger schema that podTemplateEnv/defaultPodSecurityContext correctly map to real pod-wide Tekton API fields. Verified live via ad-hoc TaskRuns in ocidex-ci before committing: with the fix, step logs show no cred-copy warning; a recent real pipeline pod (ocidex-ocidex-push-bbtnh-go-fmt, pre-fix) shows the warning in every step's log.

title: OCIRegistry reconciler retries CreateRegistry forever if status write fails after success
description: Discovered while diagnosing an empty artifacts page on the ocidex-dev homelab deployment. internal/controller/ociregistry_controller.go Reconcile() only calls OCIDexClient.CreateRegistry when cr.Status.RegistryID == "". If CreateRegistry succeeds but the subsequent r.Status().Update(ctx, cr) fails (conflict, API server blip, etc.), the new registryID is never persisted to the CRD. Every later reconcile sees RegistryID=="" again and calls CreateRegistry again, which now collides with the row already created in Postgres on registry_name_key (SQLSTATE 23505) and fails forever — the CRD never reaches Ready and no scans are ever queued. All 6 OCIRegistry CRDs in ocidex-dev were stuck like this for ~31 days. Related to ocidex-01v (K8s operator + CRDs, now closed).
acceptance_criteria: Reconcile is idempotent even if the status write after a successful CreateRegistry fails: either persist RegistryID immediately/atomically with creation, or on a create conflict look up the existing registry by name and adopt its ID instead of erroring forever.
notes:
Files: db/queries/registry.sql, internal/repository/{repository.go,registry.sql.go}, internal/service/registry.go, internal/api/{registry.go,types.go,router.go}, pkg/client/{client.go,registry.go,fake_client.go,types.go}, internal/controller/ociregistry_controller.go, plus tests in registry_test.go / ociregistry_controller_test.go / middleware_test.go.
Approach: Added GetRegistryByName (DB query -> repo -> service -> new GET /api/v1/registries/by-name/{name} endpoint -> Go SDK method). Service Create() now returns ErrConflict on a unique-violation (via existing isUniqueViolation helper) instead of a generic 500. Controller Reconcile() catches ocidexclient.ErrConflict on CreateRegistry, looks up the existing registry by spec.Name, and adopts its ID (condition reason 'Adopted') instead of retrying CreateRegistry forever. If the by-name lookup also fails, the original conflict error still surfaces. Covered by TestRegistryCreate_UniqueViolationReturnsConflict, TestRegistryGetByName_*, TestOCIRegistryReconciler_CreateConflictAdoptsExisting, TestOCIRegistryReconciler_CreateConflictLookupAlsoFails. Full unit suite (make test) and package build pass; make lint has pre-existing unrelated failures in other files (license.go, auth.go, etc.) not touched by this change.

title: Fix postgres 18 docker-compose volume mount layout
description: docker-compose.yml mounted the named volume at /var/lib/postgresql/data (old-style child path). Postgres 18+ images fatally reject any mount at that path — they require a single mount at the parent /var/lib/postgresql so the major-version subdirectory scheme can live there. This broke local docker compose startup after the postgres image was bumped to 18.4 via Renovate.
acceptance_criteria: docker-compose.yml mounts db-data at /var/lib/postgresql (parent); docker compose up brings postgres to healthy and migrate completes without the previous fatal 18+ layout error
notes:
Files: docker-compose.yml
Approach: Changed postgres service volume mount from db-data:/var/lib/postgresql/data to db-data:/var/lib/postgresql. Also cleaned up an orphaned anonymous volume (the postgres image's own implicit VOLUME declaration at /var/lib/postgresql) that was silently shadowing real leftover PG18 data at the old path and caused the error to persist even after the named db-data volume was manually deleted. Verified: docker compose up -d brings postgres to healthy, migrate runs cleanly to version 46, and /health + /ready return ok.
close_reason: Fixed volume mount path for postgres 18 layout; verified stack starts healthy

title: Refine global table + interaction CSS in index.css
description: Implement the refined field-guide spec from ADR-0023 in web/src/index.css: sort-affordance styling, row hover/motion (150ms), sticky headers, consistent density, unified empty/loading treatment. Extend existing tokens only. Run make frontend-lint-fix then make frontend-lint.
notes:
Files: web/src/index.css, web/src/components/DataTable.css

Approach:
- thead th: position:sticky; top:0; z-index:2; background:var(--color-surface) (matches card/group-header token).
- tbody tr: added transition: background-color 150ms ease (sitewide hover convention).
- tr.group-header-row td: added z-index:1 so thead (z-index:2) always wins stacking (Artifacts.tsx grouped table).
- DataTable.css: th.th-sortable:has(.sort-arrow) keeps text at full --color-text while active-sorted; .sort-arrow colored --color-accent-amber. No TSX change needed — DataTable.tsx only renders .sort-arrow for the active sortKey column.

Deviation from ADR-0023 literal text (important): the ADR assumed thead sticky would work against page/viewport scroll with 'no new scroll container' since .table-wrapper only had overflow-x:auto. Empirically verified via Playwright that this is wrong: per the CSS overflow spec, overflow-x:auto with overflow-y left as visible forces the browser to compute overflow-y as auto too, making .table-wrapper the sticky containing block — but since it had no bounded height, scrollHeight==clientHeight, so there was never any internal scroll for sticky to react to (thead top tracked window.scrollY 1:1, i.e. completely non-functional).

Fix (approved by user via AskUserQuestion, chose 'Bound table-wrapper height' over dropping sticky): added max-height:70vh; overflow-y:auto to .table-wrapper, making it a genuine internal scroll region. This changes UX for every .table-wrapper table sitewide (Artifacts, Components, Vulnerabilities, Licenses, PackagesTab, admin tables): tables now scroll internally within a 70vh box rather than the whole page. Re-verified sticky + group-header z-index stacking correctly after the change (Playwright: thead top stays fixed under internal scroll, group-header-row stays under thead).

Verified: PackagesTab.tsx does not use group-header-row (only Artifacts.tsx does) — ADR's reference to PackagesTab for that interaction was imprecise; no stacking regression there, just standard sticky-header-in-bounded-wrapper behavior.

Verification: make frontend-lint-fix + make frontend-lint clean (0 errors, 2 pre-existing unrelated warnings). Real-browser Playwright verification of sticky pin, active-sort coloring, hover transition, and group-header/thead stacking on light theme.

Follow-up worth considering: ADR-0023's 'no new scroll container' claim in the Table & interaction refinement section is now inaccurate and should be amended to describe the bounded-height wrapper.
close_reason: Sticky headers, row hover transition, group-header z-index, and active-sort styling implemented in index.css/DataTable.css; bounded .table-wrapper height added to make sticky actually function (ADR assumption was empirically wrong). Lint clean, browser-verified.

title: Git enricher — GitHub client + Enrich
description:
Implement Enrich(): read oci-metadata source info, fetch the commit from GitHub, marshal metadata to JSON.

MODIFY internal/enrichment/git/git.go:
- Options: WithTokenResolver(func(ctx context.Context, host string) string) (mirrors oci.WithCredentialResolver) and WithHTTPClient(*http.Client) for test injection.
- Enrich(ctx, ref):
  1. sourceURL, revision, err := reader(ctx, ref.SBOMId); on err return err.
  2. host,owner,repo,ok := parseSourceURL(sourceURL); if !ok or revision=="" return json {"resolved":false,"reason":"..."} with NO error (stored status=success).
  3. if host != "github.com": return {"resolved":false,"reason":"unsupported host"}.
  4. GET https://api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits/{revision} with Authorization: Bearer <token from resolver> when non-empty, Accept: application/vnd.github+json. Handle 404/403/rate-limit as an error result.
  5. Marshal output struct to JSON: host,owner,repo,commitSha,commitURL(html_url),authorName,authorEmail,authoredAt,committerName,committerEmail,committedAt,messageSubject(first line of message),parents([]sha),resolved:true.

Define a minimal GitHub commit response struct (only the fields used) — do not pull in a GitHub SDK.

TEST: httptest.Server returning a canned commit JSON; assert parsed output. Cover unresolved-source and unsupported-host paths (no HTTP call). Cover 404 -> error result.

Verify: make test. Depends on story 3.
notes:
Files: internal/enrichment/git/git.go, internal/enrichment/git/git_test.go
Approach: Implemented Enrich() using the OCIDataReader seam from .3. Reads sourceUrl/revision, parses via parseSourceURL, fetches GitHub commit via GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits/{revision} (Accept: application/vnd.github+json, optional Bearer token via TokenResolver). Unresolvable source (bad URL/missing revision/non-github host) -> JSON {resolved:false, reason} with nil error (dispatcher marks status=success, matches oci/provenance soft-failure convention). GitHub HTTP failures (404/403/decode) and OCIDataReader errors -> real Go error (status=error). Added unexported baseURL field (default https://api.github.com) mutated directly in white-box tests against httptest.Server, per user decision to avoid a third public option. title: Skip re-hydrating unchanged vuln records using querybatch modified timestamps
description:
batchResult (internal/vuln/client.go) parses each vuln modified timestamp but queryChunk discards it; hydrate then performs GetVuln + upsert + reference-replace for every unique ID on every cycle, serially. For a changed ecosystem like npm that is thousands of sequential GETs per 6h cycle for records that have not changed.

Fix: propagate (id, modified) pairs from QueryPurls; in hydrate, skip GetVuln/upsert/ref-replace when the stored modified_at is >= the reported modified (bulk lookup of stored modified_at values, e.g. a GetVulnerabilityModifiedAts query over ids). Keep mapping replacement as-is since fixed_version derivation needs the record — for skipped records reuse stored data or keep existing mapping rows. Files: internal/vuln/client.go, refresh.go, db/queries/vulnerability.sql.
acceptance_criteria: A refresh where all records are unchanged performs zero /v1/vulns/ GETs (asserted via the fake in refresh_test.go) while purl mappings remain correct. make check passes.
notes:
Files: internal/vuln/client.go, refresh.go, store.go, db/queries/vulnerability.sql, internal/repository/vulnerability.sql.go
Approach: QueryPurls now returns map[string][]QueryRef (ID+Modified) instead of map[string][]string. hydrate partitions IDs via bulk GetVulnerabilityModifiedAts lookup into toFetch (new/changed, still calls OSV GetVuln) vs toLoad (unchanged, reconstructed from stored raw JSON via GetVulnerabilitiesRaw). Verified: full test suite + race detector pass, TestHydrateSkipsUnchangedRecords asserts zero GetVuln calls on an all-unchanged cycle with correct fixed-version mappings preserved. No sqlc drift.
close_reason: Verified pre-existing uncommitted implementation: build, full test suite (race), and sqlc generate all clean; committed as 5ab4a47

title: Scheduled incremental refresh never covers new purls in unchanged ecosystems
description:
Incremental mode (selectChangedPurls) only queries purls whose ecosystem CSV advanced. A purl first seen via SBOM ingest is covered only by the ingest-time extension; if that lookup fails (2-minute timeout, network blip) or INGEST_VULN_LOOKUP_ENABLED=false, the purl stays unknown until its ecosystem CSV happens to advance — potentially days for quiet ecosystems.

Fix: in selectChangedPurls (internal/vuln/refresh.go), union in purls that have no package_vulnerability rows (add a global ListUnknownComponentPurls query modeled on ListUnknownSBOMComponentPurls in db/queries/vulnerability.sql). Note: purls with zero vulns also have no rows, so they get re-queried each cycle — acceptable until a known-clean state exists (see the purl_vuln_state backlog item).
acceptance_criteria: With all ecosystem CSVs unchanged, a purl absent from package_vulnerability is still included in the scheduled refresh query set. Unit test in refresh_test.go. make check passes.
notes:
Files: db/queries/vulnerability.sql, internal/repository/vulnerability.sql.go (generated), internal/vuln/refresh.go, internal/vuln/store.go, internal/vuln/refresh_test.go
Approach: Added ListUnknownComponentPurls SQL query (global version of ListUnknownSBOMComponentPurls); wired it through Store interface and PGStore; selectChangedPurls now always unions in unknown purls before the early-return check. Extracted mergePurls helper to keep cyclomatic complexity at 15. New test TestSelectChangedPurls_IncludesUnknownPurls verifies a purl with no mappings is included when no ecosystem CSV changes.

title: Withdrawn OSV records are stored and displayed
description:
Record.Withdrawn (internal/vuln/client.go:35) is parsed but never checked anywhere. Withdrawn records returned by querybatch keep purl mappings and remain in the vulnerability table indefinitely, showing up in counts and lists.

Fix: in hydrate (internal/vuln/refresh.go), treat a non-empty withdrawn as a tombstone: delete the vulnerability row (FK cascades clean up package_vulnerability and vulnerability_reference) or at minimum skip it and exclude it from the returned records map so replaceMappings drops its mappings. Test with a withdrawn fixture in refresh_test.go.
acceptance_criteria: A record with withdrawn set produces no vulnerability row and no purl mappings after refresh; previously-stored withdrawn records are removed on next refresh. make check passes.
notes:
Files: internal/vuln/refresh.go (hydrate guard), internal/vuln/store.go (PGStore.DeleteVulnerabilityByID), db/queries/vulnerability.sql (DeleteVulnerabilityByID query), internal/repository/vulnerability.sql.go (generated), internal/vuln/refresh_test.go (two new tests)
Approach: Added withdrawn check in hydrate after GetVuln; calls DeleteVulnerabilityByID (FK cascades) then continues past the record so it is excluded from the records map and thus from replaceMappings refs. Zero new lint issues.

title: fixed_version can come from the wrong package or release branch
description:
fixedVersionForPurl / firstFixedVersion (internal/vuln/refresh.go:435-517) scan ALL affected[] entries of a record without matching affected.package against the queried purl. Multi-package advisories (common for GHSA monorepos) and per-release Debian/Alpine affected entries can yield another package or branch fixed version. Non-SEMVER (ECOSYSTEM) ranges always fall through to firstFixedVersion, compounding this.

Fix: filter affected entries to those whose package purl (base, version-stripped) matches the queried purl before range matching; when no confident match exists, store an empty fixed_version rather than a possibly-wrong one. Add table-driven tests including a multi-package record. ECOSYSTEM-range version comparison is out of scope (follow-up).
acceptance_criteria: A record affecting two packages yields the matching package fixed version for each purl; unmatched cases store empty fixed_version. Table-driven tests added. make check passes.
notes:
Files: internal/vuln/refresh.go, internal/vuln/refresh_test.go
Approach: Added purlBase/filteredAffected helpers; fixedVersionForPurl now filters rec.Affected to purl-matched entries before searching for a fixed version. Returns empty string when no confident match. Extracted firstFixedVersionFrom([]Affected) to work on pre-filtered slices. Added semverRangeType constant (goconst). All existing tests updated to add Package.Purl to affected entries; new table-driven TestFixedVersionForPurlFiltersAffectedByPackage covers multi-package advisory, no-match, and no-purl cases.

title: Incremental refresh: apk purls gated on Alpine CSV only — Wolfi/Chainguard advisories missed
description:
purlTypeToEcosystem (internal/vuln/ecosystem.go) maps apk -> Alpine, but apk purls carry the distro in the namespace (pkg:apk/wolfi/..., pkg:apk/chainguard/... — OSV ecosystems Wolfi and Chainguard). A new Wolfi advisory does not bump Alpine modified_id.csv, so incremental refresh never re-queries Wolfi purls. Same class: deb -> Debian only (Ubuntu missed). Directly relevant: this deployment images are Wolfi-based (apko-cicd).

Fix: make the mapping return multiple candidate ecosystems per purl type (apk -> Alpine+Wolfi+Chainguard; deb -> Debian+Ubuntu); a type counts as changed if ANY of its CSVs advanced; keep per-ecosystem state rows as today. While there, add missing single mappings (cran -> CRAN, conan -> ConanCenter, bitnami -> Bitnami) — unknown types currently always refresh so those are efficiency only. Files: internal/vuln/ecosystem.go, internal/vuln/refresh.go (selectChangedPurls), tests.
acceptance_criteria: With Alpine CSV unchanged and Wolfi CSV advanced, apk purls are included in the refresh set; ecosystem state rows updated per ecosystem. Unit tests cover multi-ecosystem types. make check passes.
notes:
Files: internal/vuln/ecosystem.go, internal/vuln/refresh.go, internal/vuln/refresh_test.go
Approach: Changed purlTypeToEcosystem from map[string]string to map[string][]string. selectChangedPurls now iterates all ecosystems per type and sets anyChanged if any CSV advanced. Added Wolfi+Chainguard to apk, Ubuntu to deb, and missing cran/conan/bitnami mappings. PurlTypeToOSVEcosystem renamed to PurlTypeToOSVEcosystems. Two new tests verify apk included when Wolfi advances and excluded when all unchanged.

title: BUG: ArtifactDetail signingStatus always empty string
description:
The GET /api/v1/artifacts/{id} endpoint returns signingStatus: "" (empty string) for all artifacts, even those where the list endpoint (GET /api/v1/artifacts) correctly returns a non-empty aggregated value (e.g. "verified" or "unsigned").

Surface: The new Signing field added to the ArtifactDetail About card (ocidex-hfi.8) always shows 'Unsigned' regardless of actual signing status, because it reads from ArtifactDetail.signingStatus which is always empty.

Evidence: curl /api/v1/artifacts returns signingStatus=verified for fbba00cd (ocidex-api), but curl /api/v1/artifacts/fbba00cd returns signingStatus="". All versions in VersionsTab correctly show 'Verified' because they read from ArtifactVersionSummary.signingStatus (a separate field populated differently).

Fix: The artifact detail handler (or its service layer) needs to aggregate signingStatus across the artifact's SBOMs/versions, the same way the list handler does. Check internal/service/ and internal/repository/ for the query that backs GET /api/v1/artifacts/{id} vs GET /api/v1/artifacts and align them.
notes:
Files: db/queries/artifact.sql (GetArtifact), internal/repository/{artifact.sql.go,repository.go}, internal/service/search_artifact.go, tests/integration_test.go
Approach: GetArtifact SQL selected no signing_status, so the detail service left ArtifactSummary.SigningStatus empty (''). Added the identical aggregated provenance CASE subquery used by ListArtifacts to GetArtifact, regenerated sqlc (GetArtifactRow gains SigningStatus), updated the ArtifactRepository interface return type, and populated SigningStatus in GetArtifact service. API passes service.ArtifactDetail through directly and the type already embeds the field via ArtifactSummary, so no API/openapi/frontend changes. Added TestArtifactDetailSigningStatusParity (integration, docker-gated) asserting list and detail endpoints return the same value after seeding a verified provenance enrichment. Verified: go build/vet clean, unit tests pass, changed files lint-clean (64 pre-existing lint issues unrelated, confirmed present on baseline). Integration test not run locally (no docker).

title: fix(ci): go-test cache redundant restore + never-updated archive
description:
go-test runs after go-build on the same shared workspace PVC. Its restore step deletes and re-extracts from the cached archive (which go-build saved with build-only deps), then go-test downloads test-only deps. The save step skips because the archive already exists — so the complete cache is never persisted.

Fix:
1. restore step: skip extraction if .go-mod already exists (seeded by go-build)
2. save step: remove the 'exists, skipping' guard so go-test always overwrites with the complete (build + test) cache
notes:
Files: .tektonic/shared.ts, .tektonic/jobs/go-test/spec.ts, .tekton/tasks/go-test.k8s.yaml, .tektonic/package-lock.json
Approach: Added goCacheTest = {...goCache, forceSave: true, skipRestoreIfPathsExist: true} in shared.ts. go-test/spec.ts now imports goCacheTest. skipRestoreIfPathsExist was added to tektonic library (pvc-backend.ts, gcs-backend.ts, task.ts, task.test.ts — commit 81df6b2). make tekton-synth regenerates go-test.k8s.yaml correctly; manual YAML patches no longer needed.
close_reason: go-test cache now skips restore when go-build has seeded workspace, force-saves test deps. Implemented in tektonic library and consumed in ocidex.

title: feat: keyless verification via sigstore-go
description: Implement the keyless verification_mode using Fulcio certificate chains and Rekor transparency log. Requires sigstore-go integration. DB schema already has trust_identity and trust_issuer columns reserved for this.
notes:
Implemented on branch feat/keyless-verification (ocidex). Summary:

## Shipped
- Registry domain/service/API/CRD plumbing for trust_identity/trust_issuer end
  to end (Registry struct, RegistryService.Create/Update, CreateRegistryInput/
  UpdateRegistryInput/RegistryResponse, OCIRegistrySpec CRD fields +
  regenerated deepcopy/CRD manifest/pkg/client), mirroring how trust_public_key
  already flowed. verification_mode enum now accepts "keyless" end to end
  (was capped at none/public_key on the input side). Added a 400 validation
  guard requiring both trust_identity and trust_issuer when mode=keyless.
- TrustResolver refactored from (mode, pemKey string) to a TrustConfig struct
  carrying Mode/PublicKeyPEM/Identity/Issuer (internal/service/registry.go,
  internal/enrichment/provenance/provenance.go). BuildTrustLookup updated and
  covered by new tests.
- New internal/enrichment/provenance/keyless.go: Fulcio cert + Rekor
  transparency-log verification via sigstore-go (github.com/sigstore/
  sigstore-go v1.2.2, new dependency). Per the plan's decisions:
  - Trust root: live TUF fetch against the public-good Sigstore CDN
    (root.FetchTrustedRoot()), cached 24h in-process, degrading to a stale
    cached root rather than failing closed on a transient TUF error.
  - Rekor verification is fully offline: parses the complete
    dev.sigstore.cosign/bundle annotation (SET + canonicalized body +
    integratedTime + logID/logIndex) into a sigstore-go TransparencyLogEntry
    — no live call to rekor.sigstore.dev on any verification.
  - trust_identity is a regex matched against the Fulcio cert SAN
    (verify.NewSANMatcher), trust_issuer is an exact match
    (verify.NewIssuerMatcher).
  - Verifies both the cosign simplesigning (MessageSignature) path and the
    DSSE attestation path when present, ANDing the results, mirroring
    applyVerification's public-key contract. Fails closed (nil/false, never
    silently skips) on any parse/crypto error.
  - Added SignerIdentity/SignerIssuer to the Provenance struct so the UI can
    show *which* identity/issuer a keyless verification matched
    (ProvenanceCard.tsx now renders "Verified — keyless (issuer: ..., identity: ...)").
- Frontend: RegistriesTab.tsx keyless mode + identity/issuer fields, trust.ts/
  client.ts/queries/registries.ts updated for the new mode and fields.
- Tests added: keyless_test.go (buildTlogEntry parsing, certificate identity
  construction, guard clauses, fail-closed-on-infra-error), BuildTrustLookup
  tests in registry_test.go, validateVerificationConfig tests in
  internal/api/registry_test.go. Full existing suite (go test -short ./...,
  frontend typecheck/lint) passes; the one pre-existing frontend test failure
  (Artifacts.test.tsx "library" multi-match) and the ~65 pre-existing
  golangci-lint findings both reproduce identically on main before this
  branch — confirmed via git stash comparison, not caused by this work.

## Known gap — needs validation before this is trusted in production
The Fulcio+Rekor cryptographic verification path in keyless.go has NOT been
exercised against a real keylessly-signed artifact end-to-end (e.g. actually
verifying ghcr.io/dexidp/dex, or a test image signed live with
`cosign sign --yes` against a real GitHub Actions OIDC token). Unit tests
cover parsing/guard-clause/fail-closed behavior with synthetic data, but
building a full valid Fulcio cert chain + Rekor SET fixture for a true
happy-path crypto test was out of scope for this pass. Before relying on this
for real registries:
1. Point a test OCIRegistry at a real keylessly-signed image with
   verification_mode=keyless and confirm signing_status flips to "verified".
2. Confirm the enrichment-worker's outbound network policy in homelab allows
   the TUF fetch to tuf-repo-cdn.sigstore.dev (new egress requirement; Chains
   itself already talks to the public-good Fulcio/Rekor instance per
   talos-cluster/flux/apps/tekton-chains/chains.yaml, so this is consistent
   with existing trust boundaries, but is a new *destination*).

## Not done (explicitly out of scope per the approved plan)
- ocidex-atd.13 (drift/expiry detection) remains blocked on this ticket and
  should be picked up next — its design doc already anticipates this
  ticket's `cfg.Identity`/`cfg.Issuer` shape.

## Update: refactored to use cosign as a library instead of hand-rolled bundle construction
Per review, replaced the custom Fulcio/Rekor bundle assembly (buildTlogEntry,
verifyKeylessMessageSignature, verifyKeylessDSSEAttestation — hand-parsing
the dev.sigstore.cosign/bundle annotation into a sigstore-go protobuf Bundle)
with github.com/sigstore/cosign/v2's own cosign.VerifyImageSignatures /
VerifyImageAttestations, passed the same TrustedMaterial + digest reference +
remote.Options our own discovery already builds. cosign.CheckOpts.Identities
natively supports the SubjectRegExp/Issuer matching we need, and Offline:true
gives the same no-live-Rekor-call guarantee.

This resolves the "known gap" noted above: the crypto verification path is
now cosign's own well-tested pipeline (the reference implementation other
tools like Kyverno's policy-controller use as a library for this exact
check) rather than bespoke, fixture-untested bundle construction. Net -200
lines; go.mod grew by only +13 net lines since cosign shares almost all of
sigstore-go's transitive dependency tree already. golangci-lint issue count
returned to the exact pre-branch baseline (65) — zero new lint debt.

Still outstanding: manual end-to-end validation against a real
keylessly-signed image, and confirming homelab's enrichment-worker network
policy allows the TUF fetch to tuf-repo-cdn.sigstore.dev.

## Update: real crypto integration tests added — "known gap" resolved
Added fixture-based integration tests using sigstore-go's ca.VirtualSigstore
(an in-memory Fulcio CA + Rekor log used by sigstore-go's own test suite) —
exercises the actual cosign verify pipeline end-to-end (real cert issuance,
real ECDSA signing, real Rekor SET verification, identity/issuer matching)
with zero network dependency. See TestApplyKeylessVerification_* in
keyless_test.go.

Building this fixture caught two real bugs that guard-clause tests alone
never would have:
1. ClaimVerifier was never set on cosign.CheckOpts — meaning digest binding
   was never actually checked, so a signature valid for one image would
   have verified against any other digest. Fixed with
   cosign.SimpleClaimVerifier / IntotoSubjectClaimVerifier. Locked in via
   TestApplyKeylessVerification_TransplantedSignatureFails.
2. Switched to building an oci.Signature from our own already-fetched bytes
   (via cosign's oci/static package) and calling the singular
   VerifyImageSignature/VerifyImageAttestation, instead of letting cosign
   redundantly re-fetch from the registry. Fixes a double-fetch and is what
   made the fixture-testing possible without a fake registry.

Remaining before production trust: only the homelab TUF-egress network
policy check (tuf-repo-cdn.sigstore.dev) — the crypto correctness gap is
now closed with real, passing tests, not just unit-level guard clauses.
close_reason: Implementation complete and tested (build/vet/test/lint all pass, real crypto integration tests via sigstore-go's VirtualSigstore fixture). Closing now per decision: final field validation (real keylessly-signed image, homelab TUF egress network policy) will happen after feat/keyless-verification is merged and deployed; follow-up bugs will be filed then if issues surface.

title: feat: signed-SBOM drift detection (Direction B)
description: Detect when a previously verified SBOM can no longer be verified — e.g. key rotation, signature expiry, or registry artifact deletion. Surfaces as a status change in the UI.
design:
Branches from feat/keyless-verification (atd.15's TrustConfig/applyKeylessVerification
are hard prerequisites; atd.15 is closed in beads but not yet merged to main).

## Correction from original design: signature expiry isn't a real case
Confirmed by reading pkg/cosign/verify.go:919-920 (vendored source): cosign checks
Fulcio cert validity against the Rekor-attested signing time, not wall-clock time —
correct Sigstore design, short-lived certs shouldn't invalidate old signatures. A
keyless-verified image never "expires" on its own. Collapsed the three original
triggers into two real ones + one catch-all reason:
- trust_config_changed — key rotation OR identity/issuer edits (verification_mode/
  trust_public_key/trust_identity/trust_issuer differs from what's recorded in the
  prior Provenance JSON's SignerFingerprint/SignerIdentity/SignerIssuer).
- artifact_missing — registry deletion.
- reverification_failed — catch-all (e.g. rare Sigstore trusted-root rotation).

## Drift model
New append-only table provenance_drift_events (sbom_id, previous_status, new_status,
reason, previous_data, new_data, detected_at). enrichment table is upsert-only
(one row per sbom_id+enricher_name) so history lives separately. signing_status
gains terminal state artifact_missing (CASE expr in db/queries/artifact.sql, enum
doc on ArtifactVersionSummary.SigningStatus in internal/api/types.go:419).

## Trigger 1 — Registry artifact deletion
provenance.go Enrich() swallows all discover() fetch errors into empty
RawArtifacts{} — deleted image and never-signed image look identical. Fix:
explicit remote.Head(digestRef, opts...) existence check before discover().
404/MANIFEST_UNKNOWN -> RawArtifacts.ArtifactMissing = true (new field, threaded
through parse.go's Provenance struct), skip discovery. Any other Head error ->
return as Enrich() error (transient, job queue retries).

## Trigger 2 — Trust config changed
Already naturally re-evaluated: both applyVerification (public_key) and
applyKeylessVerification (keyless) re-verify against the trust resolver's
*current* config on every Enrich() call — confirmed in shipped atd.15 code.
Only need the comparison/recording logic below.

## Drift comparison hook
dispatcher.go processSubject() does a blind UpsertEnrichment per enricher. For
enricher_name=="provenance" (mirror existing `if e.Name() == "oci-metadata"`
special-case at dispatcher.go:178):
1. GetEnrichment(ctx, sbomID, "provenance") *before* upsert to capture prior row.
2. After upsert, derive signingStatus(data []byte) string for old vs new.
3. If old status was verified/signed and new differs, classify reason
   (artifact_missing / trust_config_changed / reverification_failed) and insert
   a provenance_drift_events row (new db/queries/provenance_drift.sql +
   InsertProvenanceDrift sqlc query).
4. Publish event.ProvenanceDrift on the existing bus. No subscriber needed yet;
   atd.14's fleet dashboard is a natural future consumer.

## Periodic recheck scheduler
Jobs only enqueued once, on event.SBOMIngested via submitter.go. Add new ticking
scheduler modeled on internal/scanner/poller.go's shape. New file
internal/enrichment/reverify.go. Config: ProvenanceRecheckInterval, default 24h
(configurable). Each tick: query SBOMs whose latest provenance enrichment is
status='success' and updated_at older than the interval (new query
ListSBOMsDueForProvenanceRecheck in db/queries/enrichment.sql), re-enqueue via
existing service.EnrichJobService.Enqueue(...) path. Wire into
cmd/enrichment-worker/main.go startup.

## API surfacing
Add only the *most recent* drift event to the per-version provenance response
(full history deferred to atd.14). Extend Provenance type (internal/api/types.go,
web/src/api/client.ts's hand-maintained interface) with optional
previousStatus/statusChangedAt.

## UI
ProvenanceCard.tsx: warning banner when previousStatus differs from current.
Extend trustStatus/badge mapping in trust.ts for artifact_missing.

## Tests
- provenance_test.go: remote.Head existence check (missing/transient-error/present).
- dispatcher_test.go: drift row inserted on status change with correct reason,
  not inserted when unchanged, scoped to provenance enricher only.
- New scheduler: unit-test extracted poll/isDue logic directly.

## Verification
1. make check on feat/drift-detection (stacked on feat/keyless-verification).
2. Manual: rotate trust_public_key, trigger recheck, confirm drift row
   reason=trust_config_changed + UI banner.
3. Manual: delete image from registry, trigger recheck, confirm
   signing_status=artifact_missing + drift row reason=artifact_missing.

Full plan: /Users/patrickfenerty/.claude/plans/ok-start-with-a-zazzy-pony.md
notes:
Implemented on branch feat/drift-detection (stacked on feat/keyless-verification,
not yet merged to main). Summary:

## Shipped
- New provenance_drift_events table (append-only; enrichment table is
  upsert-only so history has to live separately). signing_status gains a new
  terminal state artifact_missing (db/queries/artifact.sql CASE expr x3,
  internal/api/types.go enum doc).
- Trigger 1 (registry deletion): explicit remote.Head existence check in
  provenance.go's Enrich() before sig/att discovery. 404 -> ArtifactMissing:true
  on the Provenance struct, discovery skipped entirely. Any other Head error
  surfaces as a transient Enrich() error (job queue retries), not
  misclassified as deletion.
- Trigger 2 (trust config changed): no enricher change needed — both
  applyVerification and applyKeylessVerification already re-verify against
  the trust resolver's current config on every Enrich() call.
- Drift comparison hook in dispatcher.go's processSubject(): captures the
  prior successful "provenance" enrichment via GetEnrichment before the
  UpsertEnrichment, and on meaningful status change inserts a
  provenance_drift_events row. Reason classification (new
  internal/enrichment/provenance_drift.go): artifact_missing if the new data
  says so; trust_config_changed if the recorded signer (fingerprint, or
  identity+issuer) is unchanged between old and new but the verification
  outcome differs; reverification_failed as the catch-all otherwise (e.g.
  the signature itself disappeared from the registry, or a rare Sigstore
  trusted-root rotation).
- Periodic recheck scheduler (internal/enrichment/reverify.go): hourly tick,
  ProvenanceRecheckInterval config (default 24h) controls how stale a
  successful provenance check must be before requeue.
- API: SBOMDetail gains an optional provenanceDrift field (most recent event
  only — full history deferred to atd.14, though the table retains it).
- UI: ProvenanceCard.tsx shows a banner when a drift event exists; trust.ts
  handles the new artifact_missing status.
- Tests: 6 new dispatcher drift tests, 4 Reverifier tests, 2 new provenance
  existence-check tests (artifact missing / transient error). Full suite,
  vet, and lint all pass — lint issue count is actually BELOW the 65
  baseline (64) since fixing two gocyclo violations this change would have
  worsened (Enrich, GetSBOM) via the same extraction pattern used in
  ocidex-atd.15's CreateRegistry also happened to fix GetSBOM's pre-existing
  violation.

## Real design correction from the original ticket scope
Re-grounded against how atd.15 actually shipped (not the original
speculative plan) and found cosign checks Fulcio cert validity against the
Rekor-attested signing time, not wall-clock time — so keyless signatures
never expire on their own. Dropped "signature expiry" as a distinct trigger;
collapsed key rotation + identity/issuer edits into trust_config_changed.

## Real bug caught mid-implementation
The original design assumed re-enqueuing via the existing
EnrichJobService.Enqueue path for periodic recheck. That path does a plain
INSERT gated by a permanent UNIQUE (sbom_id, enricher_name) idempotency key
set at initial ingest — a second call for an already-processed SBOM would
silently no-op forever (isUniqueViolation swallows the error), meaning
periodic re-verification would never actually run. Fixed by adding
RequeueSucceededEnrichmentJob, which resets the existing 'succeeded' row
back to 'queued' instead of inserting a new one — reusing the same
state-machine pattern RetryEnrichmentJob already uses for failed jobs.

## Not done / deferred
- Full drift history UI (only the latest event is surfaced) — atd.14's
  fleet dashboard is the natural place for this.
- event.ProvenanceDrift bus event — dropped from scope entirely since no
  subscriber exists yet and every other event type in this codebase has a
  concrete consumer wired up in the same body of work that introduced it.
  Add it when atd.14 actually needs to subscribe.

Script: (1) extract VERSION by stripping release/ prefix from $(params.source-branch), (2) git config user.email/name for the bot, (3) git add CHANGELOG.md && git commit -m chore: release ${VERSION}, (4) git tag ${VERSION}, (5) git push origin HEAD:$(params.source-branch) to update the branch with the changelog commit, (6) git push origin ${VERSION} to publish the tag. Uses the existing github-cli PAT secret (mount as git credential via GIT_ASKPASS or .netrc). needs: [gitCliff]. image: alpine/git or similar. Runs before imageBuildTagTask and helmRelease so they see a consistent semver in the remote. Parent epic: plan-d5t
notes: Blocked on tektonic-wq6 (expose source-branch param) before implementation.
close_reason: Superseded by local nu release script. The script handles git-cliff, CHANGELOG.md commit, tag creation, and push. CI only builds and publishes.

Tags: vX.Y.Z, X.Y, X, and latest only when version contains no hyphen (stable releases). Requires tektonic source-branch param (tektonic issue). needs: [goTest, openapiCheck]. Parent epic: plan-d5t
notes: Blocked on tektonic-wq6 (expose source-branch param) before implementation.

title: Add git-cliff task to ocidex release pipeline

title: Prod: 3x scanner throughput — postgres CPU, +1 replica, concurrency=2

Memory limit on scanner-worker bumped to 1.5Gi to fit two concurrent Syft processes. CPU limit on scanner-worker bumped to 1500m to avoid throttling.
notes: Files: k8s/overlays/prod/patches/{resources,replicas,env-prod-scanner}.yaml. Verified via kubectl kustomize. Postgres limits 200m/512Mi → 1000m/1Gi; scanner limits 500m/1Gi → 1500m/1.5Gi; scanner replicas 2→3; SCANNER_MAX_CONCURRENCY 1→2. Net effect: 3 pods × 2 concurrent scans = 6 in-flight (was 2).

notes:

title: fix: preserve original started_at on scan job retry, track last_attempt_at
description: StartScanJob was overwriting started_at on every redelivery, losing the original start time and resetting the timeout clock. Add last_attempt_at column, use COALESCE to preserve started_at, and fix TimeoutScanJobs to use last_attempt_at.
notes:
Files: db/migrations/00028_scan_job_last_attempt.sql, db/queries/scan_jobs.sql, internal/service/job.go, internal/api/types.go, internal/api/jobs.go, web/openapi.json, web/src/types/openapi.d.ts
Approach: Added last_attempt_at column. StartScanJob now uses COALESCE(started_at, now()) so the original start time is preserved across retries; last_attempt_at tracks when the current attempt began. TimeoutScanJobs uses COALESCE(last_attempt_at, started_at) so the timeout window resets per attempt, not per original enqueue. Exposed last_attempt_at in API response.

title: dev-up doesn't stop conflicting docker-compose containers
description: The legacy docker-compose dev flow (make run / embedded mode) binds host ports 5432, 4222, 5000, 8080, 3000 — all of which Tilt also port-forwards from the cluster. Because postgres in docker-compose.yml has a restart policy, it gets auto-started on Docker daemon start and silently blocks Tilt's postgres port-forward with 'address already in use'. dev-up should stop the docker-compose stack as a preflight.
notes:
Files: Makefile (dev-up target)
Approach: Added a preflight to dev-up that detects a running docker-compose stack ([ -n "$(docker compose ps -q)" ]) and runs 'docker compose stop' before starting Tilt. The two flows share host ports (5432, 4222, 5000, 8080, 3000) so they can't coexist; postgres in particular has a restart policy that brings it back on Docker daemon start, silently re-binding 5432.

title: dev-up/dev-down don't handle stale tilt processes
description: make dev-up fails with 'address already in use' when a tilt process is already running — either a suspended foreground job from Ctrl-Z or an orphaned daemon from a prior session. make dev-down only runs 'tilt down' (which removes cluster resources) and never terminates the long-running tilt process, so it accumulates. Both targets should detect and clean up stale tilt processes.
notes:
Files: Makefile (dev-up, dev-down targets)
Approach: Added a preflight to dev-up that detects existing tilt processes (pgrep -x tilt) and stops them with SIGTERM, falling back to SIGKILL after 5s. dev-down now runs tilt down first to clean up cluster resources, then kills the long-running tilt process the same way (previously dev-down only ran tilt down, leaving the daemon orphaned). Handles both stale-from-prior-session daemons and suspended foreground jobs (Ctrl-Z).

title: dev-cluster-down leaves stale talos/kube contexts
description: make dev-cluster-down removes Docker resources but not entries in ~/.talos/config or ~/.kube/config. On subsequent dev-cluster-up, talosctl renames the new context (ocidex-dev → ocidex-dev-2), so the Makefile's hardcoded --context ocidex-dev step targets a dead endpoint and fails.
notes:
Files: Makefile (dev-cluster-down target)
Approach: Added shell loops after the docker cleanup that strip stale ocidex-dev[-N] entries from talosctl config and kubectl config (contexts, clusters, users). Awk extracts the context name from talosctl config contexts handling the '*' current-context column. Also manually pruned existing stale entries and renamed the live ocidex-dev-2 (talos) / admin@ocidex-dev-3 (kube) contexts back to canonical names so the current cluster keeps working.

title: docker/api/Dockerfile only ships /ocidex; worker binaries are missing
description:
docker/api/Dockerfile builds cmd/ocidex, cmd/scanner-worker, and cmd/enrichment-worker in the build stage but only copies /ocidex into the distroless runtime stage. The K8s worker Deployments use 'args: ["/scanner-worker"]' / '["/enrichment-worker"]' which the container then passes as an arg to the ENTRYPOINT /usr/local/bin/ocidex. Result: 'workers' silently run the API binary on port 8080 — they appear Ready, never consume from NATS, and look like dead workers in any distributed-mode test.

Fix: either (a) COPY all three binaries into the runtime image and remove the hard-coded ENTRYPOINT in favour of CMD that the manifest's args replaces, or (b) consolidate to a single binary that dispatches on the first positional argument. (a) keeps the deployments correct as written.

Surfaced during ocidex-pww (local Talos + Tilt dev loop) end-to-end bring-up.
close_reason: Fixed via multi-target Dockerfile (docker/Dockerfile) and per-service image builds: ocidex-api, ocidex-scanner-worker, ocidex-enrichment-worker. Each image ships only its own binary; deployments reference the matching image. Verified end-to-end: scan jobs now move queued → running → succeeded.

title: Local Talos + Tilt dev cluster for tight inner-loop K8s development
description: Add a local-cluster dev workflow so we can deploy ocidex to Kubernetes, edit code, and see changes redeployed without round-tripping through an external registry. Uses talosctl-provisioned Talos cluster (parity with homelab), a host-side Docker registry mirror, and a Tiltfile to orchestrate build/push/deploy on save. Adds Postgres + dev secrets to the existing k8s/overlays/dev kustomization so 'make dev-up' brings up the entire stack.

- tilt/talos-cluster.yaml — Talos config patch for localhost:5005 registry mirror at 10.5.0.1
- k8s/overlays/dev/postgres.yaml — Postgres Deployment+Service (emptyDir, dev creds)

Approach:

- Local registry is plain registry:2 in a Docker container; Tilt's default_registry pushes to it.

- Frontend stays as Vite local_resource (HMR is far better than rebuild loops); only Go services run in cluster.
- Postgres is a 1-replica Deployment with emptyDir; API auto-runs goose migrations on startup so no init container needed.
- Secrets via kustomize secretGenerator (disableNameSuffixHash=true so ocidex-secrets stays the literal name the base manifests reference). OAuth+session-secret stubbed for dev.

title: Jobs tab: error detail collapses on every data refresh
description:
In Admin > Jobs, clicking 'View error' on a failed job opens a <details> element showing the error text. However, useListScanJobs has refetchInterval: 2500, which triggers a full table re-render every 2.5 seconds. Because <details> is an uncontrolled element in Solid, each re-render resets it to its default closed state, collapsing the expanded error immediately.

**Root cause:**
The <details> element in the Last Error column (Admin.tsx:944–950) is uncontrolled HTML. Solid's reconciliation replaces the DOM node on each query result update, losing the open attribute.

**Fix:**
Replace the uncontrolled <details> with a controlled expand/collapse using createSignal per job row. Track a Set or Map of expanded job IDs in the JobsTab component, and use a Show + button pattern instead of <details>/<summary>.

Example approach:
- In JobsTab, add: const [expandedErrors, setExpandedErrors] = createSignal(new Set<string>())
- In the row: replace <details> with a button that toggles the job id in the set, and a Show component that renders the error text when the id is present
- Use untrack or a stable keyed accessor so the signal survives the query update

**Affected file:**
- web/src/pages/Admin.tsx — JobsTab, the 'Last Error' column cell (lines ~943–951)
close_reason: replaced uncontrolled <details> with Set<string> signal in JobsTab scope; expanded state survives query refetches

title: Architecture switcher shows duplicates for Windows multi-arch SBOMs
description:
## Problem

When clicking into a Windows multi-arch artifact version (/sboms/{id}), the architecture switcher shows duplicate buttons (e.g., "amd64", "amd64", "amd64", "arm64"). Same problem appears in the Architectures column of the artifact detail Versions table.

## Evidence

- Arch switcher (web/src/pages/SBOMDetail/index.tsx:276-290) renders one button per sibling SBOM with the same subjectVersion. No dedup on architecture.
- Scanner ociExpandIndex (internal/scanner/catalog.go:360-380) parses each manifest in an OCI image index but stores only arch. Windows multi-arch indexes contain multiple manifests sharing architecture: amd64 but differing in os.version.
- ociGetImageMetadata (internal/scanner/catalog.go:391-470) reads only config.Architecture — same problem.
- Result: multiple SBOMs per Windows variant; identical architecture enrichment; UI renders each as a separate "amd64" button.

## Root cause

Scanner and enrichment discard os and os.version. No qualifier capable of distinguishing Windows variants.

## Fix direction (two layers)

1. Scanner/enrichment: capture os and os.version alongside architecture. Option (a): extend enrichment record with explicit os/os.version fields, update SBOM list query. Option (b): composite platform string (e.g., windows/amd64/10.0.17763) when os == windows.
2. Frontend defense: dedupe arch siblings by platform identifier in SBOMDetail/index.tsx:276-290 and SBOMsTab.tsx:178-194.

## Affected files

- internal/scanner/catalog.go
- internal/enrichment/ (oci-metadata enricher)
- db/queries/artifact.sql (if option 1a)
- web/src/pages/SBOMDetail/index.tsx
- web/src/pages/ArtifactDetail/SBOMsTab.tsx
notes: Files: internal/enrichment/oci/oci.go, web/src/pages/SBOMDetail/index.tsx\nApproach: Two-layer fix. (1) Enricher: added platformArchitecture() helper that builds composite 'windows/amd64/10.0.17763' string when OS=windows and os.version is present, using cfg.OSVersion from go-containerregistry v1.ConfigFile. Stored in enrichment JSONB architecture field; SQL queries unchanged. (2) Frontend: archSiblings() now deduplicates by architecture using a Set — handles existing SBOMs re-enriched before this fix and any edge cases.

title: jobqueue has no non-retryable-error concept; every failure burns MaxAttempts
description:
internal/jobqueue/worker.go calls queue.FailOrRequeue(jobID, err, MaxAttempts) for every handler error, so a permanently-unscannable input costs the full retry budget (3 attempts by default) before landing in 'failed'. There is no way for a handler to signal 'this will never succeed, fail now'.

Surfaced by ocidex-ptj2: cosign .sig artifacts each burned 3 scan attempts. That specific cause is now filtered at catalog-walk time, but anything the filter misses (or any future permanent scan error) still pays 3x.

Fix direction: define an errors.Is-able sentinel in internal/jobqueue that handlers wrap. On a permanent error the worker passes maxAttempts=0 to the EXISTING FailOrRequeue query.

CORRECTION to the original filing: no db/queries change and no 'make generate' are needed. Both fail queries branch on 'attempts >= max_attempts', and every claim query increments attempts BEFORE the processor runs, so attempts >= 1 > 0 and maxAttempts=0 already yields exact permanent-fail semantics (state='failed', finished_at=now()) on the first attempt. internal/service/job.go and internal/service/enrichjob.go are also untouched.

Affects: internal/jobqueue/worker.go, internal/jobqueue/permanent.go (new), internal/scanner/engine/permanent.go (new), internal/scanner/engine/dispatcher.go.
notes:
Files: internal/jobqueue/permanent.go (new: ErrPermanent + Permanent()), internal/jobqueue/worker.go (failNow const + errors.Is branch in run(), 'permanent' log field), internal/scanner/engine/permanent.go (new: isPermanentScanError), internal/scanner/engine/dispatcher.go (wrap at ProcessOne), tests: internal/jobqueue/worker_test.go, internal/scanner/engine/permanent_test.go, tests/permanent_failure_test.go.

Approach: Permanent(err) = fmt.Errorf('%w: %w', ErrPermanent, err) so errors.Is matches both the sentinel and the cause, and last_error keeps a 'permanent: ' prefix. Worker.run passes maxAttempts=0 (failNow) on a permanent error; the existing FailOrRequeue query's 'attempts >= max_attempts' branch then fires on the first attempt because the claim query already incremented attempts. No db/queries or sqlc change.

Classification lives at engine.Dispatcher.ProcessOne (single chokepoint for the NATS hint path and the DB poll loop, and covered by dispatcher_test.go, unlike main.go). Two cases: substring 'unsupported layer media type' (syft exports no error type) and *transport.Error 404 via errors.As, with a 'MANIFEST_UNKNOWN' substring fallback since stereoscope may not preserve the typed error. Negatives (401/429/5xx, connection refused, deadline exceeded) are pinned as retryable — a transient blip misread as permanent would silently drop a scannable image.

Enrichment gets the mechanism but no classifier; enrichment.Dispatcher.processSubject stores enricher errors as status='error' rows and only propagates transient DB failures. The integration test still pins the enrichment_jobs fail query, since the shared mechanism assumes both queries stay structurally identical.

Side effect noted, no action: --once mode (ADR-027) surfaces the 'permanent: ' prefix in its exit error. Harmless — K8s Job backoffLimit governs there, not the retry budget.

Verified: make check EXIT=0, and go test ./tests/ -run TestFailOrRequeue_Permanent green (both scan and enrichment, incl. the transient control case).

title: Apply the cgroup OOM watchdog to semgrep-sast
description:
semgrep-sast is report-only (reportOnlyStatusReporter, failOnError: false) but an OOMKill defeats that entirely: Tekton treats OOMKilled as an infrastructure failure, not a script exit code, so it bypasses onError: continue, hard-fails the TaskRun AND the PipelineRun, and the appended report-status step never runs — leaving the GitHub check stuck on 'pending' rather than red.

Not hypothetical: .tektonic/jobs/semgrep/spec.ts documents a full-repo push scan OOMKilling at a 3Gi limit (semgrep-4pf); the limit is now 4Gi with no watchdog.

go-vulncheck/spec.ts:58-88 already solves this for its own task with a cgroup watchdog that polls memory.current against memory.max and self-terminates the child at 92%, converting a would-be OOMKill into a normal non-zero exit. Lift that into .tektonic/script-lib.ts as a shared snippet alongside goSetup/pacBaseline and apply it to both tasks.
acceptance_criteria: semgrep-sast under a deliberately low memory limit exits non-zero via the watchdog instead of the pod being OOMKilled; report-status runs and posts failure; the pipeline stays green.
notes: Files: .tektonic/script-lib.ts (new memoryWatchdog), .tektonic/jobs/go-vulncheck/spec.ts, .tektonic/jobs/semgrep/spec.ts. Approach: lifted govulncheck's cgroup watchdog into a shared helper. The watchdog body is POSIX sh in a raw string, so nushell values cross over as positional args (`^sh -c $watchdog semgrep ...$baseline` read back as "$@") — nu interpolation is unavailable inside r#'...'#. Verified: real semgrep run through the watchdog produced SARIF with all steps exit 0; the same generated watchdog against a memory hog at a 512Mi limit logged 'exceeded 92% of cgroup limit ... self-terminating' and terminated Completed exit=99, NOT OOMKilled. Commit 4f5c30b.

title: Make uploadSarifStep genuinely exit-neutral
description:
.tektonic/shared.ts:160-221. The comment claims the step 'ALWAYS exits 0 so a failed/again-throttled upload never flips the task's own scan verdict', but only the happy path reaches the trailing 'exit 0'. Any raise before it — a truncated or malformed SARIF failing 'open --raw'/'from json', a missing ^gzip — is caught by tektonic's wrapper, becomes rc=1, and is math max'd into the scanner's accumulated exit code. Net effect: the SCAN check goes red because the upload broke.

Inverse of silent-green (a false red misattributed to the scanner), but same root: the step's real outcome and its reported outcome disagree.

Fix: wrap the body so every path reaches exit 0, matching what the comment already claims, while still logging why the upload failed.
acceptance_criteria: A truncated semgrep.sarif makes the sarif-upload step log the parse failure and leave /tekton/home/.exit-code at the scanner's own verdict.
notes: Files: .tektonic/shared.ts uploadSarifStep. Approach: body moved into `def main []` with the skip path returning instead of exiting, wrapped in try/catch so every path reaches the trailing exit 0. Newly load-bearing: tektonic v1.3.0's report-status maxes over per-step exit codes including this step's, so an upload failure would have reddened the scan check. Verified: generated script run against a truncated semgrep.sarif logs 'error - Error while parsing JSON text' and exits 0; skip path exits 0; happy path exit 0 in-cluster. Commit 4f5c30b.
