title: make seed targets a zot registry on localhost:5000 that no dev path provides
description:
scripts/seed.nu defaults zot_addr to localhost:5000 and does 'oras copy --to-plain-http <public image> localhost:5000/...' for each of its 19 seed images. Nothing serves a registry there: docker-compose.yml has no zot service (only an orphan 'zot-data' volume at line 224), and the Tilt dev loop's registry is ocidex-dev-registry on localhost:5005, which is Tilt's image registry and not a seed target.

Result: 'make seed' exits 0 while skipping all 19 images ('oras copy failed'), so it silently seeds nothing. Exit 0 on a total no-op is the worst part — it looks like it worked.

Found while verifying the Tilt dev loop end to end for ocidex-1bbp. Unrelated to that fix (Postgres + schema); it is broken on the docker-compose path too, and predates it. docs/K8S_DEV.md and config/zot/ both still describe seeding as if zot exists.

Acceptance: 'make seed' against a running dev stack either seeds artifacts that are then queryable via /api/v1/artifacts, or fails loudly with an actionable message. Decide whether zot comes back as a dev-loop service or seed.nu is repointed/rewritten.
notes:
Files: scripts/seed.nu (rewritten), scripts/add-public-registries.nu (deleted), Makefile, docs/K8S_DEV.md, README.md

Approach: add-public-registries.nu had effectively superseded seed.nu, so folded it in and deleted it. seed.nu now registers verified public repos via POST /registries, triggers scans, polls /api/v1/artifacts, and fails loudly (non-zero) if nothing lands. Dropped oras/zot mirroring entirely; zot remains a supported registry TYPE, only the dev-loop service target is gone.

Tag globs measured against live tag lists through the real Registry.MatchesTag: 45 images / 11 repos. Two rules learned: (1) use '?' for the patch digit — 'v3.7.*' matched 78 traefik tags incl. Windows/-ea/-rc variants, path.Match has no negation; (2) tag_patterns OR across every repo in an entry, so only group repos sharing a version line (dropped skopeo and 3 flux controllers for collisions).

VERIFICATION GAP: live end-to-end against a running stack was NOT run — host disk is at 100% (1.6GiB free) and docker buildkit fails with I/O errors / corrupt content store. Verified instead against a purpose-built stub API (scratchpad/stub/main.go): create 201, re-run 409->resolve->rescan idempotency, scan 202 loop, artifact poll success, and the no-artifacts timeout failure. Both no-key and unreachable-API failure paths exit 1 with actionable messages. Glob table verified via a throwaway Go test using Registry.MatchesTag against live 'oras repo tags' output. make lint clean, make test 0 failures.

Follow-up filed for the live run.

title: Audit report-only tasks for silent-green failures
description:
Twice now a task has reported green while failing outright: ocidex-es6 (nushell 'exit 1' bypassing tektonic's try/catch, leaving .exit-code at 0) and ocidex-qzz2 (nine push steps exiting 2 behind onError: continue, invisible because nothing aggregated them).

The combination that hides failures is onError: continue plus a statusReporter with failOnError: false. That pairing is legitimate — report-only scans must not gate a release — but it means the ONLY signal is whatever the script itself emits. A task that logs nothing on failure is indistinguishable from one that passed.

Audit which tasks are report-only (start with reportOnlyStatusReporter users in .tektonic/shared.ts: the security scans, sbom-push) and confirm each one either raises via 'error make' or emits an unmissable summary line. Note that raising under failOnError:false reddens only that check and does not gate the pipeline — verified in ocidex-qzz2 — so there is no reason for a report-only task to swallow its failures.

Also worth a lint: grep .tektonic for 'exit 1' inside nu`` bodies and .nu files.
notes:
AUDIT RESULT (2026-08-10)

Report-only tasks = the five using reportOnlyStatusReporter (.tektonic/shared.ts:37): govulncheck-scan, grype-vuln-web, gitleaks-secrets, semgrep-sast, sbom-push.

ALL FIVE ALREADY RAISE ON FAILURE. Verified empirically that a bare ^cmd returning non-zero raises in nushell and is caught by tektonic's wrapper:
  nu -c 'def main [] { ^false }; try { main; 0 } catch { 1 }'  -> rc=1, prints 'error: External command had a non-zero exit code'
So ^gitleaks / ^semgrep --error / ^grype --fail-on high / ^sh -c watchdog all propagate. sbom-push additionally aggregates per-binary results and raises via error make (fixed in ocidex-qzz2). No report-only task is silent-green today.

THE 'exit 1' LINT PASSES. 'exit' appears only in .sh bodies (safe — Sh wraps them in a subshell and reads $?), inside the ^sh -c watchdog heredoc at go-vulncheck/spec.ts:79, and as deliberate 'exit 0' skip paths (push-sboms.nu:7, shared.ts:178/220).

FOUR GAPS FOUND, tracked under epic ocidex-im4o + tektonic:
1. Anonymous failure message — 'error: External command had a non-zero exit code' names no task, step or command. Framework-level: tektonic-epr.
2. SILENT GREEN, live: '| complete | get stdout' discards the exit code in go-fmt/fmt.nu:11 and tekton-check/spec.ts:36. gofmt exiting 2 on a parse error has empty stdout -> 'OK: all files formatted'. -> ocidex-im4o.1
3. uploadSarifStep (shared.ts:160-221) documented 'ALWAYS exits 0' but only the happy path reaches it; a malformed SARIF reddens the scan check. -> ocidex-im4o.2
4. OOMKill bypasses onError: continue entirely — hard-fails the pipeline despite report-only and leaves the check pending. semgrep-sast is exposed (OOMKilled at 3Gi per semgrep-4pf, now 4Gi, no watchdog). -> ocidex-im4o.3

ROOT CAUSE IS FRAMEWORK-LEVEL. tektonic hand-maintains /tekton/home/.exit-code inside the script, which nushell's untrappable 'exit' defeats. Probed rpi-cluster/ocidex-ci: Tekton itself writes /tekton/steps/step-<name>/exitCode for EVERY completed step, regardless of onError, mode 0644, absent only for the currently-running step. tektonic-9wr moves the capture there. Cross-repo epic: plan-t48.
close_reason: Audit complete and recorded in notes; all four gaps it identified are fixed across tektonic v1.3.0 and ocidex-im4o.

title: No task sets imagePullPolicy; mutable image tags can serve stale layers
description:
ocidex-qzz2 was caused by the kubelet's IfNotPresent default on the mutable tag ghcr.io/pfenerty/ocidex-cli:main. sbom-push no longer uses a published image, but the exposure is general: no step in the pipeline sets imagePullPolicy, and tektonic's TaskStepSpec (dist/lib/core/task.d.ts) has no such field to set.

Remaining mutable refs are goImage (ghcr.io/pfenerty/apko-cicd/golang:1.26) and syftImage (:1.45.1) in .tektonic/shared.ts. Both are version-pinned so they change rarely, but a republished tag under the same version would be served stale from a node cache indefinitely, with no signal.

Cross-repo: add imagePullPolicy to TaskStepSpec in tektonic, release, bump the dep in ocidex, re-synth. Alternative is Renovate pinDigests over the CI images, which ADR-038 currently excludes.
notes:
Files: .tektonic/pipeline.ts (defaultImagePullPolicy: Always), .tektonic/jobs/go-integration/spec.ts (postgres + nats sidecars), .tektonic/package.json + package-lock.json (tektonic v1.3.0 -> v1.4.0), 46 regenerated .tekton/tasks/*.yaml.
Approach: added imagePullPolicy support upstream in tektonic v1.4.0 (tektonic-q9k) — ImagePullPolicy type, optional field on TaskStepSpec/TaskSidecarSpec, defaultImagePullPolicy on TektonicProjectOptions merged into each task's stepTemplate. ocidex sets it once at project level; stepTemplate covers injected cache/reporter steps but NOT sidecars (Tekton excludes them), so go-integration's two sidecars set it explicitly. Digest-pinning left rejected per ADR-038 (Renovate cannot run make tekton-synth). Accepted cost: ~11-12 anonymous Docker Hub manifest requests per push/tag run vs the 100-per-6h cap.
Verified: ad-hoc TaskRun of ocidex-gofmt-check on rpi-cluster showed Always on both containers and kubelet 'Pulling image' on a warm node; TaskRun Succeeded; go-integration-test applied and read back with sidecar imagePullPolicy intact (not CRD-pruned).

acceptance_criteria: /api/v1/components?purl= filters the list. /components?purl= is linkable and renders the filtered view. No new component detail route is added.
notes:
Files: db/queries/search.sql (SearchComponents), internal/service/search.go + search_component.go, internal/api/types.go + search.go + search_test.go, pkg/client/component.go, web/src/api/queries/components.ts + index.ts, web/src/pages/Components.tsx + Components.test.tsx
Approach: SearchComponents SQL now takes name as a narg alongside a new exact-match purl narg (existing idx_component_purl serves it; matched exactly, not by prefix, so a link built from one row's purl returns every SBOM carrying that package version). name lost required:true at the API, replaced by a handler 400 when neither name nor purl is given — that keeps the unbounded-scan case rejected while making purl a first-class key. Frontend: /components splits into ComponentBrowser (unchanged distinct browse) and PurlOccurrences, selected on the purl search param, so ?purl= is linkable and renders the occurrence list; rows link to /sboms/{id} since ADR-042 R6 adds no component detail route.

title: Web resolver routes + 409 disambiguation view (ADR-042 R7)
description: Add /artifacts/lookup and /sboms/lookup routes to web/src/App.tsx. Each resolves client-side and navigate(..., { replace: true }) to the canonical UUID route on a unique match, so the back button does not trap the user on the resolver. On 409, render a disambiguation list of candidates instead of navigating; on 404, the existing NotFound.
acceptance_criteria: Sharing /artifacts/lookup?name=ghcr.io/pfenerty/ocidex lands on the artifact detail page. Back button returns to the referring page, not the resolver. 409 renders a selectable candidate list. make frontend-lint-fix then make frontend-lint clean.
notes:
Files: web/src/api/queries/lookup.ts (new), web/src/pages/Lookup.tsx (new), web/src/pages/Lookup.test.tsx (new), web/src/App.tsx
Approach: useArtifactLookup/useSBOMLookup wrap the generated openapi-fetch client with retry:false (a 409 is an answer, not a transient failure) and enabled gating on the required qualifiers. conflictCandidates()/isNotFound() decode APIClientError so the page never string-matches. Shared ResolverView component: createEffect navigates to the canonical UUID route with replace:true on unique match (back button returns to the referrer, not the resolver), renders the candidate list as links on 409, the existing NotFound page on 404, and an 'Incomplete lookup' EmptyState when the query string lacks name / digest-or-artifact+version. Routes /artifacts/lookup and /sboms/lookup declared ahead of the :id routes. 8 vitest cases mount the real router plus stub destination routes so the redirect assertion checks real navigation.

title: Copy shareable link affordance on artifact/SBOM detail
description: ADR-042 accepts that the address bar shows the UUID after resolution, which means copying from the address bar yields the non-shareable form. This is the compensating change, not optional polish: a copy-link control on the artifact and SBOM detail pages that emits the resolver URL (/artifacts/lookup?name=... , /sboms/lookup?artifact=&version=), including whatever qualifiers are needed to make it unambiguous.
acceptance_criteria: Control present on ArtifactDetail and SBOMDetail. Emitted URL includes enough R4 qualifiers to resolve to exactly one candidate. Pasting the copied URL round-trips back to the same page.
notes:
Files: web/src/components/CopyShareLink.tsx (new), web/src/components/CopyShareLink.test.tsx (new), web/src/pages/ArtifactDetail/index.tsx, web/src/pages/SBOMDetail/index.tsx, web/src/pages/Lookup.test.tsx
Approach: CopyShareLink button (lucide Link2 + existing copyText/toast) absolutises the resolver path against window.location.origin. artifactLookupPath() emits every R4 rung the record carries (name, type, group) since an omitted qualifier is a wildcard and only widens the match. sbomLookupPath() deliberately keys on digest, NOT artifact+version+arch+flavor: a rebuild yields a second SBOM sharing all four ladder values, so the ladder form would 409 for older links, whereas sbom.digest is UNIQUE and pins the record. It returns null when digest is absent (SBOMDetail.digest is optional in the schema) and the control is Show-gated on that. Round-trip proven in Lookup.test.tsx by mounting the resolver at artifactLookupPath(...) output and asserting the parsed qualifiers plus the redirect.

title: Regenerate OpenAPI + extend pkg/client with resolver calls
description: Run make openapi to regenerate web/openapi.json and web/src/types/openapi.d.ts for the three lookup endpoints, and add the corresponding methods to pkg/client (artifact.go, sbom.go) so the CLI can resolve by name.
acceptance_criteria: make openapi produces no diff on a second run. pkg/client exposes LookupArtifact/LookupSBOM/LookupLicense with the 409 candidate body surfaced as a typed error. Frontend build passes against the generated types.
notes:
Files: pkg/client/lookup.go (new), pkg/client/lookup_test.go (new), pkg/client/errors.go, pkg/client/client.go, pkg/client/fake_client.go
Approach: OpenAPI/TS/pkg-client regeneration was already done incrementally in stories .1-.3 (make check gates on openapi-check + generate-client-check); re-running make openapi && make generate-client here produced no diff, satisfying the idempotence criterion. Added LookupArtifact/LookupSBOM/LookupLicense to the Client interface, httpClient (using the generated LookupArtifactParams/LookupSbomParams; spdxID plain for license), and FakeClient. Typed 409: new ConflictError{Detail, Candidates []LookupCandidate} with Unwrap() -> ErrConflict so existing errors.Is(err, ErrConflict) checks keep working; mapError decodes the body and only returns it when candidates are present, so non-resolver 409s (duplicate registry name) stay the bare sentinel. Empty optional qualifiers are omitted from the query string rather than sent empty.

title: License lookup resolver (ADR-042 R3)
description: Add GET /api/v1/licenses/lookup?spdxId=. spdx_id is already a natural key (idx_license_spdx_id UNIQUE WHERE NOT NULL), so this is a straight lookup with no qualifier ladder.
acceptance_criteria: 200 on match, 404 on none. Handler test covers both.
notes:
Files: internal/service/search_lookup.go (LookupLicense), internal/service/search.go (interface), internal/api/lookup.go (Handler.LookupLicense), internal/api/types.go (LookupLicenseInput/Output), internal/api/router.go (lookup-license op, tagLicenses const), internal/api/lookup_test.go, internal/api/search_test.go.
Approach: no new SQL. spdx_id is already UNIQUE WHERE NOT NULL, and ListLicenses already exposes an exact spdx_id filter plus the visibility-aware component_count, so LookupLicense delegates to it with Limit 1 and maps the empty page to ErrNotFound. No qualifier ladder and no 409 is possible, so the operation declares no conflict response. Also hoisted the repeated "Licenses" tag literal into tagLicenses alongside the other tag constants.

title: SBOM lookup resolver (ADR-042 R3/R4/R5)
description: Add GET /api/v1/sboms/lookup with two forms: ?artifact=&version=&arch=&flavor= (R4 ladder: artifact+version -> +arch -> +flavor) and ?digest= (unique by construction via idx_sbom_digest, so never ambiguous). Visibility via visible_namespace_ids before counting.
acceptance_criteria: Both query forms resolve. 200/404/409 semantics per ADR-042 R5. digest form documented and tested as never returning 409. Table-driven handler tests.
notes:
Files: db/queries/sbom.sql (LookupSBOMs), internal/service/search_lookup.go (SBOMLookupQuery, LookupSBOM), internal/service/search.go (interface), internal/api/lookup.go (Handler.LookupSBOM), internal/api/types.go (LookupSBOMInput), internal/api/router.go (lookup-sbom op), internal/api/lookup_test.go, internal/api/search_test.go, regenerated openapi/client types.
Approach: one SQL query serves both forms - digest, artifact, version, arch and flavor are all optional nargs, and the handler enforces 'digest OR (artifact AND version)' with a 400. version is matched against the same COALESCE(subject_version, imageVersion) expression ListArtifactVersions builds version_key from, so a version copied out of the versions view resolves; the s.id::text fallback is omitted deliberately. artifact is LEFT JOINed since sbom.artifact_id is nullable, so a digest lookup still finds an unlinked SBOM. architecture is cast ::text so sqlc types it as string rather than interface{}. sbom_visible() applied in SQL per R5. Digest form's never-409 property is asserted across every digest in the fixture rather than one value.

title: Artifact lookup resolver (ADR-042 R3/R4/R5)
description: Add GET /api/v1/artifacts/lookup?name=&type=&group=. Repository query + service lookup implementing the ADR-042 R4 qualifier ladder (name -> +type -> +group; omitted qualifiers are wildcards, not empty-string matches). Candidates filtered through artifact_visible() BEFORE counting (R5). Handler mirrors GetRegistryByName (internal/api/registry.go:199) for the private-resource-is-404 rule.
acceptance_criteria: 200 with the artifact on a unique visible match; 404 on none; 409 with candidate list (id + distinguishing qualifier values) on more than one. Table-driven handler tests for all three outcomes alongside internal/api/registry_test.go. Test asserts a private candidate does not turn a unique public match into a 409. Test uses a slash-bearing name (ghcr.io/pfenerty/ocidex) end to end.
notes:
Files: db/queries/artifact.sql (LookupArtifacts), internal/repository/artifact.sql.go (generated), internal/service/search_lookup.go (new: LookupCandidate, ArtifactLookupQuery, searchService.LookupArtifact), internal/service/search.go (interface), internal/api/lookup.go (new: LookupConflictError, lookupConflictResponses, Handler.LookupArtifact), internal/api/types.go (LookupArtifactInput), internal/api/router.go (lookup-artifact op), internal/api/lookup_test.go (new), internal/api/search_test.go (fake method), web/openapi.json + web/src/types/openapi.d.ts + pkg/client/types.go (regenerated).
Approach: exact name match with type/group as R4 ladder rungs; NULL param = wildcard so an omitted qualifier widens rather than pins. artifact_visible() applied inside the SQL so the handler counts only visible candidates (R5). Handler returns 200 (fetches full ArtifactDetail via GetArtifact so the body matches GET /artifacts/{id}), 404, or a *LookupConflictError implementing huma.StatusError carrying the candidate list; the 409 schema is declared explicitly on the operation because huma only infers schemas from the output struct, so otherwise candidates would vanish from the generated client. Empty query values are treated as wildcards (huma cannot distinguish omitted from empty for a string param) - documented in the param doc strings and covered by a test.

title: Canonical name-keyed resource URLs (ADR-042)
description: Implement the additive name-keyed resolver scheme decided in docs/adr/0042-canonical-resource-urls.md (spike: ocidex-e86). UUID paths stay canonical; new lookup endpoints resolve human-composable name+version queries to them, returning 200 on a unique visible match, 404 on none, 409 with candidates on ambiguity.
close_reason: All 7 stories complete; ADR-042 name-keyed resolvers implemented across API, client, and web. Merged to main.

title: sbom-push should consume ghcr.io/pfenerty/ocidex-cli instead of compiling it
description:
Since ocidex-5dw, ocidex-cli ships as ghcr.io/pfenerty/ocidex-cli. The sbom-push task still compiles the CLI from source in its build-binaries step to do the pushing. Once the image exists on main, the push-sboms step can run the published image instead, dropping one binary from the compile.

Note the ordering constraint: sbom-push runs BEFORE the image-build chain in the pipeline, so it would consume the previous commit's CLI image, not the one built by the same run. That is fine for a report-only dogfooding task but should be a deliberate decision, not an accident. Note also that ocidex-cli is still a subject of the self-SBOM run and would need to stay in shippedBinaries (or be catalogued from the image).

Parent context: ADR-029 Distribution section.
notes:
Files: .tektonic/jobs/sbom-push/spec.ts (push-sboms.nu deleted), cmd/ocidex-cli/sbom.go, cmd/ocidex-cli/sbom_test.go, docs/adr/0029 + 0040, .tekton/tasks/sbom-push.k8s.yaml (synth).

Approach: push-sboms replaced by 10 generated steps on ghcr.io/pfenerty/ocidex-cli:main using command/args (distroless = no shell, so no loop and no derived values). Added --version-file/--arch-file to 'sbom push'; build-binaries now writes .sbom-bins/.version alongside .goarch. Dropped @version from --subject-purl (artifact.purl is an attribute, UpsertArtifact conflicts on type+name+group).

Premise correction: this saved NO build time. ocidex-cli stays in shippedBinaries as its own SBOM subject, so build-binaries compiles it either way (34s for all 10, warm cache). The gain is dogfooding fidelity only. Consumes the PREVIOUS commit's CLI, deliberately - gating on image-build-cli would delay upload by the ~60m image chain and skip dogfooding whenever an image build fails.

Verified: ad-hoc TaskRun test-sbom-push-8zxk7 in ocidex-ci (with podTemplate securityContext). build-binaries wrote 'version 0.0.0-12b11d22' + amd64; distroless steps pulled, ran under runAsUser 1024/runAsNonRoot, parsed args, resolved workingDir. All 10 push steps exited 2 with cobra usage - EXPECTED: :main is the previous commit's CLI and predates both new flags. Task still reported Succeeded (onError: continue), confirming the report-only contract. Self-heals on the second post-merge run.

Known regressions (documented in spec.ts): no clean skip when OCIDEX_API_KEY is unset (Tekton has no step-level when) - 10 failed-but-continued steps instead of 1 skip; no 'N of M failed' summary, failures are per-step now.

title: ocidex-ci namespace is missing webhooks.knative.dev/exclude=true
description:
CLAUDE.md § Tekton CI Dev Loop documents that the ocidex-ci namespace carries the label webhooks.knative.dev/exclude=true so that kubectl apply of task YAML bypasses the Tekton admission webhook. The label is NOT present on the cluster.

Symptom: kubectl apply -f .tekton/tasks/image-release-web.k8s.yaml is rejected with a 'non-existent variable' error on ${TAG#refs/tags/} in release.sh. The image-build-* tasks happen to apply cleanly (no parameter-expansion syntax), so the gap only shows up on the release tasks.

Found while verifying ocidex-2j2. The namespace is Flux-managed, so the label belongs in the homelab repo's namespace manifest, not applied by hand.

Fix: add the label to the ocidex-ci Namespace in homelab and let Flux reconcile; or update CLAUDE.md if the bypass is deliberately no longer wanted.
notes:
Files: homelab/talos-cluster/flux/apps/ocidex-ci/namespace.yaml (the fix), ocidex CLAUDE.md (docs)
Approach: label added declaratively in homelab (commit 5e0a2bd, homelab-jiy), Flux reconciled; live ns now carries webhooks.knative.dev/exclude=true. CLAUDE.md now points at the declarative source instead of telling you to kubectl label by hand, and records the cost: the selector is DoesNotExist, so the label disables Tekton's DEFAULTING webhook too, namespace-wide, PAC PipelineRuns included (safe — tektonic emits serviceAccountName/timeouts explicitly).
Finding: real CI was never affected. PAC inlines remote tasks as spec.taskSpec, and an embedded taskSpec with ${VAR#prefix} is admitted even without the label; only the standalone Task object is checked. Documented as the escape hatch under 'Shell variable syntax in task scripts'.
Verified: kubectl apply -f .tekton/tasks/ now applies all 43 tasks incl. the 12 image-release-* (previously denied); the in-cluster copies were 51d stale and are now at HEAD. Ad-hoc TaskRun (ocidex-gofmt-check, with podTemplate securityContext) ran green end to end.

title: NATS StatefulSet cannot run under PodSecurity 'restricted' (root image + hostPath-backed PVC)
description:
Split out of ocidex-1d9, which brought every OCIDex-built workload in charts/ocidex and charts/ocidex-operator up to the PodSecurity 'restricted' profile. NATS is the one workload left out.

Two independent blockers, both verified empirically on rpi-cluster, not reasoned about:

1. docker.io/nats:2-alpine runs as uid 0 and declares no non-root user in /etc/passwd, so runAsNonRoot needs an explicit runAsUser to be satisfiable at all.

2. The real blocker is storage. The JetStream store at /data/jetstream is created mode 0700 root:root. fsGroup does NOT fix this: the nats PVC uses the local-path storage class, which is a hostPath provisioner, and the kubelet only applies fsGroup volume ownership to volume types that support ownership management — hostPath is not one of them. Patching the live StatefulSet to runAsUser/runAsGroup/fsGroup 1000 produced:

    [FTL] Can't start JetStream: storage directory is not writable

Note this only bites on UPGRADE of an existing root-owned store. A fresh install would likely work, because local-path creates the volume root 0777 and NATS would then create jetstream/ as uid 1000 itself. Untested.

Options, roughly in order of preference:
- Move NATS to a CSI storage class that honours fsGroup, then apply the standard block.
- One-shot migration: chown the store to 1000:1000 on the node / via a privileged Job, then switch. Needs a documented upgrade step; breaks unattended upgrades.
- Adopt the upstream NATS Helm chart as a dependency and let it own its own security context.
- Accept NATS as the documented exception and enforce 'restricted' per-namespace only where NATS does not run.
acceptance_criteria: NATS runs under PodSecurity 'restricted' with its existing JetStream data intact (message and consumer counts preserved across the switch), OR a decision is recorded that NATS stays exempt and the reason is documented in charts/ocidex/values.yaml.
notes:
Files: charts/ocidex/values.yaml (nats.podSecurityContext/nats.securityContext), charts/ocidex/templates/statefulset-nats.yaml, charts/ocidex/templates/NOTES.txt

Approach: the recorded blocker was narrower than believed. Verified on rpi-cluster that /data is 0777 root:root — local-path's setup script is literally 'mkdir -m 0777 -p $VOL_DIR' — and only /data/jetstream is 0700 root:root because nats-server created it as root. So a FRESH volume works for any uid without fsGroup; only in-place upgrade over a root-owned store fails. Added nats-specific podSecurityContext (runAsNonRoot + explicit runAsUser/runAsGroup/fsGroup 1000 + RuntimeDefault) and securityContext (drop ALL, no privesc, readOnlyRootFilesystem), rendered with the same 'with' guards as every other template. NATS needs its own keys rather than the chart-wide ones because its image declares no non-root user, so runAsNonRoot needs an explicit numeric uid.

Rejected the issue's option 1 (CSI class honouring fsGroup): rpi-cluster has only local-path (hostPath) and nfs-client (NFS), neither of which the kubelet applies fsGroup to, so it would mean installing a new CSI driver in homelab — and NFS is a poor JetStream backend. Rejected option 3 (upstream NATS chart) as disproportionate for a single-replica doorbell broker. Rejected a privileged chown Job as self-defeating (the Job itself breaks 'restricted').

The issue's acceptance criterion 'message and consumer counts preserved' was dropped deliberately: it tests a property the architecture does not have. The store is a doorbell cache, not the queue of record (ADR-024) — internal/nats/client.go:64 provisions the stream with CreateOrUpdateStream and internal/jobqueue/worker.go:50 documents PollInterval as the DB poll fallback. Chose PVC recreation over migration.

Verification (all live on rpi-cluster, before commit): helm template + kubectl apply --dry-run=server into a scratch ns enforcing restricted:latest = ZERO warnings (was exactly one, on the nats container); negative control with both keys nulled restores all four violations, proving the check has teeth. Live swap on ocidex-dev: scaled to 0, deleted PVC, patched sts, scaled up -> uid=1000, /data/jetstream created drwx------ 1000:1000, JetStream started, no FTL, readOnlyRootFilesystem confirmed working (touch /etc failed as expected). Stream + 6 consumers re-provisioned after a rollout restart; the 7th (enrichment-hint, 27 pending) was a dead pre-ADR-033 consumer, correctly not recreated.

NEW FINDING folded into NOTES.txt: wiping the PVC is not sufficient on its own. Running pods reconnect but never re-provision the stream, because CreateOrUpdateStream only runs at process startup — streams stayed at 0 until a rollout restart. The upgrade note now makes the restart a required second step and explains why work is still not lost (DB poll fallback). Proved the fallback empirically: inserted a queued scan_jobs row with no NATS hint and the worker claimed it on its poll tick.

Cluster left at the target state deliberately. Flux was resumed and reconciled green, but Helm's three-way merge kept the live securityContext (the old chart never managed that field). Left in place rather than reverted: reverting would let root write new files into the now-1000-owned store and re-break the upgrade when the chart ships. Test scan_jobs row deleted, psa-scratch ns deleted.
close_reason: NATS now runs under restricted with an explicit uid; existing installs recreate the PVC (store is a doorbell cache, not the queue of record). Verified live on rpi-cluster with a negative control. Follow-ups: ocidex-gsip (P1 scanner regression found while testing), ocidex-9yq4 (helm lint in CI).

title: docs: INGESTION.md section 3 is stale (422 vs 400, phantom user enrichment write)
description:
Two inaccuracies found while fixing ocidex-784:

1. Section 3 says mandatory-validation failures return 422. They return 400: validateContainerRequired/validateUploadRequired return *service.ValidationError, which mapServiceError (internal/api/errors.go) renders as huma.Error400BadRequest. Only validateBOM (internal/api/sbom.go) returns 422, for bomFormat/specVersion/empty-components.

2. It documents an UpsertEnrichment(enricher_name='user') write inside the ingest transaction that service.Ingest no longer performs.
acceptance_criteria: docs/INGESTION.md section 3 states the correct status code per validation gate and no longer describes the 'user' enrichment write.
notes:
Files: docs/INGESTION.md
Approach: Section 3 now states 400 for all service-layer validation gates (resolveArtifact missing-digest, validateContainerRequired, validateUploadRequired -> *service.ValidationError -> mapServiceError -> huma.Error400BadRequest) and adds a '400 vs 422' subsection scoping 422 to the handler-level validateBOM (bomFormat/specVersion/empty components). Documented the previously-missing validateUploadRequired gate (ADR-040). Rewrote 'Transaction contents' to match service.Ingest: InsertSBOM -> linkArtifactNamespace -> insertBOMContent (insertComponentsBatch + insertDependencies) -> Commit; the UpsertEnrichment(enricher_name='user') step is gone. Post-commit section now names the full SBOMIngested payload (incl. Architecture/BuildDate) and the root-enricher enqueue (user, oci-metadata, provenance) via enrichment.NATSSubmitter. Matching fixes in section 5 ('populated synchronously' -> async user enricher) and section 6 diagram (422 -> 400; enrichment[user] moved into the async block).

title: Migrate operator env vars into OperatorConfig
description: cmd/operator/main.go still reads OCIDEX_SERVER, OCIDEX_API_KEY and OPERATOR_NAMESPACE with raw os.Getenv plus inline empty checks, while every other operator setting goes through config.LoadOperator. Deliberately left out of ocidex-1eo to keep that fix scoped to the finalizer bug. Moving them into OperatorConfig makes them testable in TestLoadOperator alongside WatchNamespaces and the leader-election timings, and puts all startup validation in one place.

title: Home: artifact-type breakdown tile
description:

Adding one requires backend work: a new sqlc query in db/queries/stats.sql, a field on DashboardStats (internal/service/search.go), the stats-warmer snapshot path and the scoped-stats variant, the API type in internal/api/types.go, then 'make openapi' before any frontend change is possible.

notes:
Files: db/queries/stats.sql (GetArtifactTypeCounts), internal/service/search.go (ArtifactTypeCount DTO + DashboardStats field), internal/service/search_stats.go (8th errgroup aggregate + buildDashboardStats mapping), internal/api/types.go + search.go (ArtifactTypeCountEntry, artifact_types), web/src/pages/Home.tsx + Home.css (chip row), web/src/pages/Artifacts.tsx (useSearchParams type filter). Warmed out-of-band with the other seven aggregates (no request-path cost). Dev cluster was down, so the plan's Tilt E2E was replaced with tests/stats_types_test.go: seeds two containers in a public namespace and one application in a private one, then asserts anonymously that container==2, application==0 and the chips sum to artifact_count, and again as admin that application==1 — proving the exclusion is visibility, not the type going unreported. ArtifactsRouting.test.tsx mounts the real @solidjs/router because the stubbed Artifacts.test.tsx proves only the component's half of the useSearchParams contract.

title: image-build-web takes 13m47s, the longest in the chain
description: Measured in push-t2t4l (2026-08-05): web is 13m47s of the 61m ten-image chain, nearly 2x the next slowest. Unlike the Go images it builds from docker/web/Dockerfile and shares no builder-base with them, so the persistent buildkitd root from ocidex-2vr buys it much less — the npm install + vite build is repeated work that only caches against its own prior run. Worth checking whether node_modules can use a --mount=type=cache like the Go stages do, and whether the package.json/lock COPY is split from the source COPY so a source-only change does not re-run npm ci. Sibling of ocidex-2j2, which covers the Go compile side.
notes:
Files: docker/web/Dockerfile (only file changed; no .tektonic/.tekton changes needed since the Dockerfile ships in the build context, not generated task YAML).

Diagnosis: the issue's two hypotheses were already implemented — the npm cache mount (--mount=type=cache,target=/root/.npm) and the split package.json/source COPY were both already in place. The real cost was the build stage's base image. docker.io/node:24-bookworm is 390 MiB compressed / ~1.1 GiB unpacked vs 97 MiB for ghcr.io/pfenerty/apko-cicd/nodejs:24. The chain's buildkitd runs --oci-worker-snapshotter=native, which copies rather than overlays, so the base size is paid again on EVERY layer of the stage (~7-8 GiB written per cold build). The resulting ~5 GiB resident footprint then competed for the shared keepBytes=14GiB GC ceiling with the nine Go builds, so web's snapshots were evicted between runs and every run was cold.

Approach: swapped the build stage to apko-cicd/nodejs:24 (already used by eslint-lint-web and grype-vuln-web). Required USER root + explicit HOME=/root and NPM_CONFIG_CACHE=/root/.npm — the apko base sets run-as: nonroot (uid 1001) and carries no HOME, so the existing cache mount would have silently missed (the same trap the Go builder-base hit in ocidex-2j2). Also npm install -> npm ci (eslint-lint-web already runs npm ci, so the lockfile is known in sync; dropped the package-lock.json* glob so a missing lockfile fails at COPY) and npx tsc && npx vite build -> npm run build so the image and make frontend cannot drift.

Measured on-cluster with ad-hoc TaskRuns against the real ocidex-buildkit-cache root (scratch task copy pushing to ocidex-web-test5343 so the real :main tag was never touched):
  baseline push-j99c5 image-build-web (warm root, same day): 10m59s
  after, cold (apko base never in the root):                 3m39s
  after, web source changed / deps unchanged:                2m19s
  after, no change (fully CACHED):                            0m05s

Context for the baseline: in that same run the whole ten-image chain was 18m06s (api 3m22s incl. build-all, seven workers 18-37s each, web 10m59s, operator 38s) — web alone was 61% of the chain.

Functional verification: ran the built image as a pod, curl'd it — HTTP 200, index.html references index-ByNzuqnC.js / index-BnPOjeV0.css, byte-identical asset hashes to a local make frontend build. Serve stage unchanged (chainguard/nginx, uid 65532, :8080).

Note: the residual ~2m on a web-source change is the native snapshotter copying the ~650 MiB stage (base + node_modules) for the COPY web/ . and build layers. If that ever needs to go, the follow-up is to move the vite build into a Tekton task that already has the node_modules cache (eslint-lint-web does npm ci in 26s) and give the web image its own .buildctx-web context so .buildctx stays byte-identical for the nine Go builds — not needed at 2m19s.

title: make tekton-check target does not exist
description: CLAUDE.md references "make tekton-check" twice as a local gate (Tekton CI Dev Loop section and the pipeline workflow notes), but the Makefile has no such target — only tekton-synth. The drift check exists solely as the CI task .tektonic/jobs/tekton-check/spec.ts, which runs npx tsx pipeline.ts then fails if git status --porcelain -- .tekton is non-empty. Either add a Makefile target mirroring that, or correct CLAUDE.md. Note the semantics differ locally: CI runs on a clean checkout, whereas locally you legitimately have uncommitted .tekton changes mid-edit, so a naive port would false-positive. The useful local form is "synth is idempotent" (re-synth adds no new diff).
notes:
Files: Makefile (new tekton-check target + .PHONY), .tektonic/pipeline.ts (TEKTON_OUTDIR override on outdir), CLAUDE.md (Key Commands entry)

Approach: TektonicProject's outdir and repoRelativePath are independent — repoRelativePath is what
gets embedded in the YAML as remote task refs, so redirecting outdir alone yields byte-identical
output. tekton-check synthesizes to /tmp/tekton-check and diff -r's against the committed .tekton,
mirroring the existing openapi-check / generate-client-check convention. Non-mutating and
git-state-independent, unlike the CI git-status form which needs a clean checkout. The recursive
diff also catches orphaned files .tektonic no longer emits — stronger than the CI gate.

Not wired into 'make check': costs an npm ci + full synth for a rarely-changed area, and CI already
gates it behind the pipelineChanged bucket.

Verified: clean tree passes and leaves .tekton untouched; tekton-synth output unchanged (empty git
status); injected hand-edit -> make exit 2; orphan file -> make exit 2 ('Only in .tekton/tasks').

Note: the issue said CLAUDE.md referenced the target twice — only one stale reference existed
(~/code/CLAUDE.md:78, now correct since the target exists). ocidex/CLAUDE.md:269 accurately
describes the CI task, not a make target.

title: Per-binary go build is now the whole image-build cost (~210-300s each)
description: After ocidex-2vr.2 (persistent buildkitd root) and ocidex-2vr.3 (registry cache removed), builder-base is fully CACHED across images and the per-image build is dominated by go build ./cmd/<name>: 209.7s for git-worker, 296.6s for scanner-worker, out of ~315s total. The shared /root/.cache/go-build cache mount persists in the buildkit root and IS present in every per-binary stage, yet does not appear to cut the compile much across images. Worth checking whether the mount is actually shared across stages (buildkit cache mount IDs are per-target by default), and whether GOFLAGS/GOCACHE inside the builder are pointed where we think. ~35-50 min of a ten-image pipeline sits here.
notes:
Files: docker/Dockerfile, Tiltfile, .tektonic/jobs/image-build/{spec.ts,build.sh,release.sh}, regenerated .tekton/tasks/image-{build,release}-*.k8s.yaml

Root cause (confirmed twice): ghcr.io/pfenerty/apko-cicd/golang:1.26 has User=1001 and no GOPATH/GOCACHE/GOMODCACHE in its Env, so Go resolved GOCACHE=/home/nonroot/.cache/go-build and GOMODCACHE=/home/nonroot/go/pkg/mod. Both --mount=type=cache targets in the Dockerfile (/root/.cache/go-build, /go/pkg/mod) were dead paths Go never touched. Verified from the OCI config blob and from an in-cluster probe pod. Each of the nine per-binary stages therefore branched off a cached builder-base with an empty build cache and cold-compiled the whole cosign/sigstore-go graph (786 transitive deps, ADR-037) -> 210-300s apiece.

Approach:
1. docker/Dockerfile: collapsed nine build-<name> stages into one build-all that compiles all nine shipped mains in a single 'go build -o /app/bin/ ./cmd/...' (enumerated, not ./cmd/... glob -- ocidex-cli/specgen/dbcheck/backfill are not shipped). Final stages COPY --from=build-all; all nine target names unchanged so --opt target=, docker-compose and Tiltfile keep working. Also cuts native-snapshotter disk: one derived copy of builder-base instead of nine.
2. builder-base: USER root + ENV GOPATH=/go GOMODCACHE=/go/pkg/mod GOCACHE=/root/.cache/go-build, so the cache mounts are live. Throwaway stage; shipped distroless stages still run nonroot.
3. build-arg:DATE pinned to the commit timestamp via a new .buildctx.date file written by prepare-build-context. build.sh/release.sh previously passed a per-task wall-clock 'date -u', which lands in build-all's ldflags -> different RUN string per image -> guaranteed cache miss. This was found empirically: round-1 scanner-worker still took 3m56s with build-all re-running. Wall-clock CREATED still feeds OCI labels/annotations (applied at export, no effect on the build cache).
4. build-and-push limits.memory 2Gi -> 3Gi (requests unchanged); build-all links nine mains concurrently. No OOMKill observed on a full-compile run.

Measured (ad-hoc TaskRuns on the real cluster, PVC pvc-3ed245d6da, before committing):
  api            baseline 7m19s -> 6m21s cold (base re-pull) -> 34s warm
  scanner-worker baseline 5m25s -> 18s, log shows '#14 [build-all] CACHED'
End-to-end: kubectl run of the pushed test image executed its entrypoint and failed correctly on missing DATABASE_URL.

Caveats: first real run after this lands is cold (build-all stage identity + mount semantics both changed); the tag pipeline's buildkit-release-cache has never been warmed since ocidex-2vr. Tilt and 'docker compose build' now compile nine binaries per change instead of four/one, mitigated by the now-working GOCACHE. internal/version.Date now carries the commit timestamp, not the build wall-clock.

title: Operator pod violates PodSecurity 'restricted'
description:
The ocidex-operator Deployment (charts/ocidex-operator/templates/deployment.yaml) sets no securityContext, so applying it produces PodSecurity 'restricted' warnings:

  - allowPrivilegeEscalation != false
  - unrestricted capabilities (needs capabilities.drop: ["ALL"])
  - runAsNonRoot != true
  - seccompProfile unset (needs RuntimeDefault)

Surfaced by a server-side dry-run apply while debugging ocidex-vh6. Warning-only today because the ocidex-operator-dev namespace enforces a laxer level, but the pod would be REJECTED outright in any namespace that enforces restricted — which is the direction prod should go.

The operator is a plain controller-runtime binary: it needs no privileges, no host access, and no writable root beyond /tmp. There is no reason for it not to be restricted-compliant.
design:
Add to the pod spec:

  securityContext:
    runAsNonRoot: true
    seccompProfile:
      type: RuntimeDefault

and to the container:

  securityContext:
    allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
    capabilities:
      drop: ["ALL"]
    readOnlyRootFilesystem: true

Expose via values.yaml (podSecurityContext / securityContext) with these as defaults so an operator can loosen them without forking the chart, matching the resources/leaderElection pattern already in values.yaml.

No image work needed: docker/Dockerfile line 167 already builds the operator on gcr.io/distroless/static-debian12:nonroot (UID 65532), as do all nine Go runtime stages. runAsNonRoot: true will be satisfied as-is. readOnlyRootFilesystem is the only setting worth verifying at runtime — controller-runtime writes nothing to disk without webhooks configured, but confirm rather than assume.

This is chart-only, so it is a candidate to fold into the ocidex-vh6 chart work rather than a separate branch.
acceptance_criteria:
1. kubectl apply --dry-run=server of the rendered chart emits zero PodSecurity warnings.
2. The operator pod reaches Running with the new securityContext (i.e. the image genuinely runs as non-root and tolerates a read-only root filesystem).
3. Reconciliation still works end to end — an OCIRegistry/ScanRequest CR is processed after the change.
notes:
Files: charts/ocidex-operator/{values.yaml,templates/deployment.yaml}; charts/ocidex/values.yaml; charts/ocidex/templates/{deployment-api,deployment-web,deployment-scanner-worker,deployment-enricher-workers,deployment-vuln-worker,job-migrate,statefulset-nats}.yaml

Approach: chart-level podSecurityContext/securityContext values (defaulting to the restricted set) rendered with 'with' guards into every workload, following the existing resources/leaderElection convention so operators can loosen without forking. Scope was widened from operator-only to both charts on the user's call; the issue's own CORRECTION note was right that web needed no rootless rework (Chainguard nginx, UID 65532).

web needed more than the block: nginx writes /run/nginx.pid and /var/lib/nginx/tmp, so two emptyDirs are mounted, gated on readOnlyRootFilesystem so disabling the setting does not leave stray volumes.

NATS excluded, split to ocidex-s3tu. Root third-party image, JetStream store 0700 root:root, fsGroup is a no-op because the PVC is local-path (hostPath provisioner; kubelet only applies fsGroup to volume types supporting ownership mgmt). Tried live, got '[FTL] Cant start JetStream: storage directory is not writable', reverted.

Verification on rpi-cluster with a scratch ns enforcing restricted:latest: 0 violations both charts (nats the only remaining warning); negative control with values nulled still violates, proving the check has teeth; operator ran with readOnlyRootFilesystem as leader with 8 successful OCIRegistry reconciles / 0 errors; nginx served HTTP 200. All live patches reverted, scratch ns deleted, Flux resumed, no drift.

Incidental fix: deployment-web.yaml nil-deref on .Values.securityContext.readOnlyRootFilesystem when securityContext is nulled (found by the negative control). Now (default dict .Values.securityContext).

Note: the original PodSecurity warnings came from a cluster-wide PSA default, not namespace labels — ocidex-dev/ocidex-operator-dev carry no pod-security labels. Also noted: no helm lint anywhere in Makefile or .tektonic, which is why this reached a live cluster.

title: Distribute ocidex-cli: go install path + published container image
description:
`ocidex-cli` has no distribution path. `make build` compiles it to `bin/ocidex-cli` (Makefile:23) and CI builds it inside the `sbom-push` task only because it is the tool doing the pushing — that binary is discarded with the workspace. There is no Dockerfile stage, no entry in the image-build chain, no release asset, and no goreleaser config. `.tekton/tasks/gh-release.k8s.yaml` POSTs only release metadata (tag_name, name, CHANGELOG body) and attaches nothing. ADR-029 mentions installation once, in passing (line 29), and never decides how the binary gets anywhere.

Net effect: the only way to get the CLI is `git clone && make build`. Epic ocidex-e3g shipped eight subcommands nobody can install.

Two consumers, two answers:

1. Developers and CI runners with a Go toolchain — `go install github.com/pfenerty/ocidex/cmd/ocidex-cli@latest` already works incidentally because the module is public. Make it deliberate: document it in README and ADR-029.

   This drags in a prerequisite. `ocidex-cli` has no `version` subcommand at all, and `internal/version` is ldflags-only (`Version = "dev"`, version.go:5) while `make build` passes no ldflags — so nothing would report a useful version even if asked. A `go install`ed binary gets no ldflags either, but it does get module metadata, so `version` should read `debug.ReadBuildInfo()` and fall back to the ldflags vars. Without this, "which CLI is this user running" has no answer, which is a support problem the moment the binary leaves this repo.

2. In-cluster and container consumers — publish `ghcr.io/pfenerty/ocidex/ocidex-cli` alongside the other nine images, so a Tekton task or K8s Job can `ocidex-cli sbom push` without a Go toolchain. This is what `sbom-push` should eventually consume instead of compiling the CLI itself every run.
design:
Image follows the established pattern exactly — this is an eleventh instance of a shape that already exists nine times, not a new mechanism.

1. `docker/Dockerfile`: add a `build-ocidex-cli` stage mirroring `build-operator` (line 119), and a final stage on `gcr.io/distroless/static-debian13:nonroot` mirroring the operator's (line 167). Per ADR-038 the runtime base stays distroless static and stays digest-pinned by Renovate.

2. `.tektonic/jobs/image-build/spec.ts`: append one row to `imageSpecs` (line 110):
   `["ocidex-cli", "docker/Dockerfile", "OCIDex CLI", "Command-line client for OCIDex", "ocidex-cli"]`
   `serialChain` picks it up for both the push chain (`image-build-*`) and the tag chain (`image-release-*`) with no other change. Then `make tekton-synth` and check the generated `.tekton/tasks/` diff for the known cdk8s `${VAR#prefix}` drop.

3. Verify with an ad-hoc TaskRun against a recent workspace PVC before committing — never push a commit to test a pipeline change (see CLAUDE.md "Tekton CI Dev Loop").

Cost to weigh: `imageSpecs` builds serially by design (spec.ts:100 — parallel builds overcommit the node and leave pods Pending on "Insufficient cpu"). An eleventh image lengthens the push pipeline, already ~2h40m and tracked as ocidex-2vr. The CLI image is small and the registry build cache is warm, so the marginal cost is minutes, not the ~16 min average — but if ocidex-2vr lands a parallelization or path-filter change first, rebase onto it rather than adding to the serial chain.

Deliberately out of scope: goreleaser, a Homebrew tap, and attaching cross-compiled binaries to the GitHub release. `go install` covers the Go-toolchain audience for the cost of a README line; release assets only matter for users without Go, and there is no evidence of that audience yet. File a follow-up if one appears.
acceptance_criteria:
- `ocidex-cli version` exists and prints version, commit, and date, preferring `debug.ReadBuildInfo()` over the ldflags vars so a `go install` build reports its module version rather than "dev".
- `go install github.com/pfenerty/ocidex/cmd/ocidex-cli@latest` yields a working binary that passes the check above.
- README documents both install paths; ADR-029 records the distribution decision instead of assuming the binary is already on PATH.
- `docker/Dockerfile` has a `build-ocidex-cli` stage and a distroless final stage; `docker build --target ocidex-cli` succeeds locally.
- `.tektonic/jobs/image-build/spec.ts` lists ocidex-cli; `make tekton-synth` regenerates `.tekton/tasks/image-build-ocidex-cli.k8s.yaml` and `image-release-ocidex-cli.k8s.yaml`, and `make tekton-check` is clean.
- An ad-hoc TaskRun of the generated build task pushes `ghcr.io/pfenerty/ocidex/ocidex-cli` successfully — verified before the commit, not after.
- `docker run --rm ghcr.io/pfenerty/ocidex/ocidex-cli --help` lists the full subcommand surface.
notes:
Files: internal/version/version.go (+test), cmd/ocidex-cli/version.go (+test), cmd/ocidex-cli/root.go, cmd/ocidex/main.go, docker/Dockerfile, .tektonic/jobs/image-build/spec.ts, .tektonic/jobs/sbom-push/{spec.ts,push-sboms.nu}, regenerated .tekton/**, README.md, docs/adr/0029-cli-design.md.

Approach: version.Info()/String() prefer the -ldflags vars and fall back to debug.ReadBuildInfo() (Main.Version, ignoring '(devel)'; vcs.revision; vcs.time), so go install reports a real version. readBuildInfo is a var seam for tests. cmd/ocidex --version routed through version.String() so both binaries print one format. ocidex-cli gained a 'version' subcommand plus root --version/-v sharing one string via SetVersionTemplate; the subcommand declares a no-op PersistentPreRunE, which shadows the root's and so answers without resolving a config file it may exist to diagnose.

Image: ocidex-cli joined the shared build-all stage (NOT a separate stage - that would cold-compile the cosign graph again) plus a distroless 'cli' final stage. imageSpecs row is named 'cli', not 'ocidex-cli': imageEnv prefixes 'ocidex-', so the published name is ghcr.io/pfenerty/ocidex-cli, matching its ten siblings. The issue's acceptance criteria said ghcr.io/pfenerty/ocidex/ocidex-cli; that shape would need a permanent special case in imageEnv and was rejected with the user. ocidex-cli also moved into sbom-push's shippedBinaries now that it ships an image.

Verified BEFORE merge, on the real cluster: ad-hoc TaskRun of the generated ocidex-image-build-cli (with the full podTemplate) pushed ghcr.io/pfenerty/ocidex-cli:sha-e6a40ab7 and :main at sha256:4767cd49aeee. build-all was cold (expected: adding a package changes its RUN string) at ~4m43s total; the cli final stage's distroless base was CACHED. kubectl run of that digest: 'version' printed 'ocidex-cli main-e6a40ab7 (commit e6a40ab7..., built 2026-08-09T01:27:33Z)' and '--help' listed the full subcommand surface. Locally: go install ./cmd/ocidex-cli reported the pseudo-version + vcs stamps; an -ldflags build reported the injected values, confirming precedence. make fmt/lint/test/openapi-check/generate-client-check clean.

Follow-ups filed: ocidex-f2bj (pre-existing: report-status cannot write /tekton/home/.exit-code, so a failing image build could report success), ocidex-2u7y (sbom-push consuming the published CLI image).

Not done, deliberately: goreleaser, Homebrew, GitHub release assets - recorded as rejected in ADR-029.
close_reason: Shipped: go install path (build-info version fallback + ocidex-cli version cmd) and ghcr.io/pfenerty/ocidex-cli image as the 11th link in the image-build chain. Verified on cluster; merged to main in f8acbfc.

title: Broaden list and landing surfaces beyond containers
description: Artifacts.tsx gets distinct entry-card treatment per type. Home.tsx:20,80 copy ('Know what's in your containers', 'Browse tracked OCI images and Helm charts') broadens, plus an artifact-type breakdown tile. admin/RegistriesTab.tsx becomes SourcesTab, grouped by namespace, with OCI config shown only for kind='oci_registry'.
design: Add a namespace facet only if more than one namespace is visible. Registry was never a browse axis — do not add one by reflex now that it has a better-named successor.
acceptance_criteria:
- landing copy no longer implies containers only
- admin view groups sources by namespace and hides OCI config for upload sources
- Artifacts.test.tsx extended
- frontend-lint clean
notes:
Files: web/src/pages/Home.tsx, web/src/pages/Artifacts.tsx + .test.tsx, web/src/api/queries/sources.ts (new), web/src/api/client.ts, web/src/api/queries/index.ts, web/src/pages/admin/SourcesTab.{tsx,css,test.tsx} (git mv from RegistriesTab.*), web/src/pages/Admin.tsx, web/src/App.tsx

Approach:
1. Home landing copy rewritten so tagline/pitch/artifacts-card no longer imply containers only.
2. Artifacts.tsx: extractNamespace() parsed EVERY artifact name as an OCI path, so a library named 'mylib' got a one-row group heading repeating itself. Replaced with groupOf(): container -> first two path segments, else purl group, else type (rendered as a TypeBadge). Headings suppressed entirely when there is only one group. 4 new tests.
3. Admin Registries tab -> Sources tab, grouped by owning namespace (ADR-039). No backend change needed: migration 00053 makes registry.id a FK onto source.id, so /api/v1/sources (which already carries namespace_name) joins /api/v1/registries by id in a Map. New useListSources hook.
4. Upload sources get their own short list per namespace rather than rows of em-dashes in the registry table -- that would claim OCI settings exist but are unset. The columns array and the edit dialog are untouched, keeping churn and risk low.
5. /admin/registries kept as a live route alias so existing bookmarks do not 404.

Deferred (recorded, not silently dropped):
- Artifact-type breakdown tile on Home: no artifact-type aggregate exists anywhere in the stats pipeline; needs a new sqlc query + DashboardStats field + warmer + scoped variant + API type + make openapi. Filed as ocidex-l1e0.
- Entry-card redesign of the Artifacts table: story description mentions it but the binding AC only requires Artifacts.test.tsx extended. A table->card rewrite would churn 7 existing tests for no AC gain; type-aware grouping + TypeBadge delivers per-type treatment in the table idiom.

Gates: frontend-lint 0 errors (2 pre-existing warnings in Vulnerabilities.tsx:46 and utils/vuln.ts:93), tsc clean, 150/150 vitest tests pass, vite build clean. Backend untouched, so make check was not the relevant gate.

title: ADR-0038: web serving and base image policy
description: docs/adr/0038-web-serving-and-base-image-policy.md covering Chainguard nginx over Caddy, L7 routing at the Gateway, distroless-static for Go, and the digest-pinning policy including why CI images are excluded. Add to the CLAUDE.md ADR index.
notes:
Files: docs/adr/0038-web-serving-and-base-image-policy.md, CLAUDE.md
Approach: ADR follows docs/adr/template.md. Covers Chainguard nginx over Caddy with the 178->19 package evidence, L7 routing at the Gateway rather than a sidecar server (with the no-upstreams/start-time-resolution argument), distroless static-debian13 for Go, and the digest-pinning policy including why CI images are excluded. title: Move the NATS image into chart values
description: charts/ocidex/templates/statefulset-nats.yaml hardcodes docker.io/nats:2-alpine. Move to values.yaml as nats.image.{repository,tag} so Renovate helm-values manager sees it.
notes:
Files: charts/ocidex/values.yaml, charts/ocidex/templates/statefulset-nats.yaml
Approach: docker.io/nats:2-alpine was hardcoded in the StatefulSet, invisible to Renovate inside a Helm template. Moved to values.yaml as nats.image.{repository,tag} so the helm-values manager picks it up; also lets operators point at an external/managed NATS. Verified via helm template.

title: Indicate CRD-managed registries in the admin UI
description:
The operator (internal/controller/ociregistry_controller.go) creates and updates registries through the ordinary public API and records nothing CRD-specific, and the registry table has no managed-by column. Admins therefore cannot tell which registries are owned by an OCIRegistry CR - and edits made in the UI are silently reverted on the next reconcile.

Fix: add managed_by/managed_ref columns to registry (migration + db/queries/registry.sql + make generate); expose them on the registry API types (make openapi + make generate-client); populate them from specToCreateBody/specToUpdateBody in the controller; render a 'Managed by Kubernetes' badge in RegistriesTab.tsx titled with namespace/name, and guard the edit dialog so spec-owned fields are disabled with an inline explanation.
acceptance_criteria: A CRD-created registry shows the badge and a guarded edit form; a UI-created registry is unchanged; repository round-trip and RegistriesTab tests cover both
notes:
Files: db/migrations/00050_registry_managed_by.sql, db/queries/registry.sql, internal/service/registry.go(+_test), internal/api/types.go, internal/api/registry.go, internal/controller/ociregistry_controller.go, web/src/pages/admin/RegistriesTab.tsx(+.test.tsx)

Approach: added nullable managed_by/managed_ref to registry (no CHECK constraint — a Terraform provider, epic ocidex-dsy, would be a second legitimate value). Operator stamps the marker in BOTH specToCreateBody and specToUpdateBody: the adopt-on-conflict path (ErrConflict -> GetRegistryByName) never calls create, so update is the only place an adopted registry can get marked. Service Update preserves the marker when params are nil, mirroring the trust-field precedent — without it the UI's PATCH (which omits the field) would silently un-mark an operator-owned registry on the first save. Frontend: 'Managed by Kubernetes' badge titled with namespace/name, plus a warning notice and a wrapping <fieldset disabled> that locks every control and the Save button — the operator reconciles the whole spec, so every field is spec-owned and a badge alone would let an admin lose edits. Tests: four service tests (create round-trip, unmanaged leaves NULL, update preserves when nil, update overwrites when set) and RegistriesTab.test.tsx (badge present/absent, form locked/unlocked).

title: Make the vulnerabilities table sortable (server-side)
description:
/vulnerabilities already uses DataTable, but its Column<TopVulnEntry> definitions omit sortKey so no header is clickable. The page is server-paginated, so client-side sort would only order the visible 25 rows - the sort has to be server-side.

Fix: parameterise ORDER BY in ListTopVulnerabilities (db/queries/vulnerability.sql:105) keeping the current severity ordering as default; add SortBy/SortDir with enum tags to ListTopVulnerabilitiesInput (internal/api/types.go:527); wire sortBy/sortDir/onSort in Vulnerabilities.tsx following the pattern at web/src/pages/Components.tsx:156. Requires make generate, make openapi, make generate-client.
acceptance_criteria: Column headers sort; sorting issues a new query rather than reordering the visible page; make check passes including openapi-check and generate-client-check
notes:
Files: db/queries/vulnerability.sql (parameterised ORDER BY), internal/service/search_vuln.go (normalizeTopVulnSort + params), internal/service/search.go (TopVulnFilter.Sort/SortDir), internal/api/types.go + search.go (sort/sort_dir query params with enum), web/src/api/queries/vulns.ts (TopVulnSort union), web/src/pages/Vulnerabilities.tsx (sortKey per column + onSort), tests in internal/service/search_service_test.go and web/src/pages/Vulnerabilities.test.tsx.
Approach: server-side sort because the list is server-paginated. Numeric sort keys (severity rank, cvss_score, both affected counts, published_at epoch) share one ORDER BY term with the sign-flip direction trick copied from SearchDistinctComponents; canonical_id is text so it needs one term per direction. Severity/CVSS stay as tiebreakers, which keeps the default (severity desc) byte-identical to the previous hardcoded ordering. huma enum tags constrain sort_by; the service clamps again so the query never sees an unknown column. Verified all five sort columns and both directions by running the sqlc-generated SQL against the dev cluster DB (ocidex-pg-1) before committing.

title: Artifacts.test.tsx 'renders artifact type badge' fails: getByText('library') matches both the type filter option and the badge
description:
Pre-existing failure on main (reproduced by stashing all working-tree changes). web/src/pages/Artifacts.test.tsx:120 asserts getByText('library'), but the page renders a type-filter <select> whose <option value="library">library</option> now also matches, so testing-library throws getMultipleElementsFoundError.

Not caused by the signing-badge work in ocidex-xxr; found while verifying it. Fix is to scope the assertion to the badge (e.g. getAllByText and assert the span.badge, or query within the table).
acceptance_criteria: web frontend suite is green: npx vitest run reports 0 failures
notes:
Files: web/src/pages/Artifacts.test.tsx

Approach: the assertion was scoped to the whole container, so getByText('library') matched both the type-filter <option> and the row badge. Replaced it with a query over 'td span.badge' asserting one badge's textContent is 'library' — which is what the test claimed to check; the old form would have passed on the filter alone even if the row never rendered.

title: replace hand-rolled Rekor HTTP call with sigstore/rekor client; fix response body leak
description:
fetchRekorUUIDFromBase (internal/enrichment/provenance/parse.go:169) hand-rolls an HTTP request against Rekor's REST API. cosign already brings in sigstore/rekor/pkg/client and its generated go-swagger client — go-openapi is in the module graph specifically because of this.

The hand-rolled version also leaks the response body:

    resp, err := http.DefaultClient.Do(req)
    if err != nil || resp.StatusCode != http.StatusOK {
        return ""
    }
    defer resp.Body.Close()

On any non-200 it returns before the deferred Close is registered, leaking the connection. (No nil-deref risk — Go short-circuits on err != nil — but the leak is real and unbounded across sweeps.)

This code predates ocidex-82g, but the epic's cosign adoption removed the reason not to use the upstream client. At minimum fix the leak; preferably switch to the Rekor client.
acceptance_criteria: The response body is closed on every path. Rekor lookups use the upstream client, or the leak fix is accompanied by a note explaining why the hand-rolled call is retained.
notes: Files: internal/enrichment/provenance/parse.go, internal/enrichment/provenance/provenance_test.go, go.mod\nApproach: Replaced the hand-rolled http.DefaultClient.Do call in fetchRekorUUIDFromBase (which leaked the response body on non-200 responses) with the upstream github.com/sigstore/rekor/pkg/client generated client (rekorclient.GetRekorClient + entries.GetLogEntryByIndex), already in the module graph indirectly via cosign. Promoted it to a direct dependency in go.mod. Updated the malformed_json/empty_map test cases to set Content-Type: application/json on the httptest handler, matching real Rekor responses and the swagger client's content-type-driven consumer selection. All fetchRekorUUID subtests and the full enrichment package suite pass; golangci-lint and gofmt clean.

title: replace hand-rolled in-toto/SLSA structs with in-toto/attestation types
description:
internal/enrichment/provenance/parse.go defines its own inTotoStatement, inTotoSubject and slsaPredicate structs to parse attestation payloads. These are partial, hand-maintained copies of a published, versioned schema.

Since 82g.2 adopted sigstore/cosign/v2, github.com/in-toto/attestation is already in the module graph transitively — switching to in-toto/attestation/go/v1 (Statement, ResourceDescriptor) and the upstream SLSA v1 predicate types costs no new top-level dependency and removes the risk of the local structs silently failing to parse valid statements as the spec evolves.

This is the same tradeoff 82g.2 already made successfully for simplesigning (deleting simpleSigning/sigBoundDigest in favour of cosign's claim verifiers).
acceptance_criteria: parse.go uses upstream in-toto/SLSA types rather than local copies. Existing parse tests pass unchanged. No new direct dependency beyond what cosign already pulls in.
notes:
Files: internal/enrichment/provenance/parse.go, go.mod, go.sum
Approach: Replaced local inTotoStatement/inTotoSubject/slsaPredicate structs with github.com/in-toto/attestation/go/v1.Statement and go/predicates/provenance/v1.Provenance. These are protobuf-generated (structpb.Struct/timestamppb.Timestamp under the hood), so decoding requires protojson.Unmarshal rather than encoding/json (the json struct tags are cosmetic and wrong, e.g. Statement.Type is really "_type" on the wire). Added parseInTotoStatement (protojson.Unmarshal into intotov1.Statement) and applyInTotoStatement (round-trips the generic structpb.Struct predicate through protojson.Marshal/Unmarshal into the typed slsav1.Provenance, then reads BuilderID/BuildStartedOn/SourceURI/SourceCommit via nil-safe getters). extractFromRawInToto and extractFromDSSE now both call these helpers. go mod tidy promoted github.com/in-toto/attestation and google.golang.org/protobuf from indirect to direct — no new top-level dependency. All existing provenance tests (TestBuildProvenance subtests, TestDiscover_RawInToto, TestApplyKeylessVerification_RawInTotoOnlyNoSignature) pass unchanged.

title: ProvenanceCard copies props.drift into a non-reactive const
description:
web/src/components/ProvenanceCard.tsx:26:

    // eslint-disable-next-line solid/reactivity
    const drift = props.drift;
    ...
    <Show when={drift}>

This silences the solid/reactivity rule rather than fixing what it flagged. In SolidJS, destructuring or copying a prop breaks the tracking scope: the card will not re-render when drift data arrives or changes after first render.

Use props.drift directly in the Show and remove the disable comment. Per CLAUDE.md, run 'make frontend-lint-fix' then 'make frontend-lint' afterwards.
acceptance_criteria: No eslint-disable for solid/reactivity in ProvenanceCard.tsx. The drift banner appears when drift data loads after initial render. make frontend-lint passes.
notes:
Files: web/src/components/ProvenanceCard.tsx
Approach: Removed the const drift = props.drift; snapshot and its eslint-disable, using props.drift directly in the <Show when={props.drift}> check so SolidJS's tracking scope sees prop reads and re-renders the drift banner when drift data arrives after initial render. make frontend-lint-fix / make frontend-lint both pass with 0 errors (2 pre-existing warnings in unrelated files).

title: hand-written deepcopy file is named zz_generated.* and will be clobbered
description:
api/v1alpha1/zz_generated.deepcopy_extra.go (127 lines) is hand-written but carries the generated-file naming convention and the '//go:build !ignore_autogenerated' tag. It holds the manual TrustIdentity/TrustIssuer deepcopy additions.

The zz_generated prefix and build tag both signal 'controller-gen owns this'. CLAUDE.md explicitly instructs not to edit zz_generated files. Someone will regenerate and lose this code, or edit it and have it overwritten.

Rename to deepcopy_manual.go, drop the misleading build tag, and add a comment explaining why these methods are not generated.
acceptance_criteria: The file no longer uses the zz_generated naming convention or the ignore_autogenerated build tag. 'make generate-operator' leaves it untouched and the build still passes.
notes: Files: api/v1alpha1/zz_generated.deepcopy_extra.go -> deepcopy_manual.go\nApproach: Renamed via git mv to drop the zz_generated naming convention; removed the //go:build !ignore_autogenerated tag; replaced header comment with an explanation that these DeepCopyInto/DeepCopy methods for OCIRegistrySpec/OCIRegistryStatus/ScanRequestStatus/APIKeyStatus are hand-written because controller-gen v0.21.0 calls them but doesn't emit them, and must be kept in sync manually. Verified make generate-operator leaves the file untouched (only .beads/issues.jsonl and the git-mv rename show in git status) and go build/vet/test pass.

title: testIgnoreSCT package global wired into production CheckOpts
description:
internal/enrichment/provenance/keyless.go declares 'var testIgnoreSCT bool' at package scope and reads it directly when constructing production cosign.CheckOpts:

    baseOpts := cosign.CheckOpts{ ..., IgnoreSCT: testIgnoreSCT }

A mutable package global that weakens signature verification is a poor test seam: it is not concurrency-safe across parallel tests and nothing prevents production code from setting it.

Move it onto the enricher/verifier struct or into trust.Config so it is explicit and scoped.
acceptance_criteria: No package-level mutable global controls verification strictness. Tests inject the setting through a struct field or config value.
notes:
Files: internal/enrichment/provenance/keyless.go, internal/enrichment/provenance/keyless_test.go, internal/enrichment/provenance/provenance.go
Approach: Removed the package-level 'var testIgnoreSCT bool' and its mutate/restore pattern in tests entirely. Added ignoreSCT as an explicit bool parameter to applyKeylessVerification instead. The one production call site (Enricher.applyTrust in provenance.go) hardcodes false -- there is no legitimate production path that can ever set it true. Tests that use ca.VirtualSigstore (which never embeds an SCT) now pass true explicitly as a function argument at each call site. This is stronger than moving the flag onto a struct field: it's not shared mutable state at all, so there's no concurrency hazard between parallel tests and no risk of it leaking into a production code path via any config or option.

notes:

title: drop duplicate cosign bundle struct in favour of cbundle.RekorBundle
description:

Delete the local struct and use cbundle.RekorBundle throughout.

notes:
Files: internal/enrichment/provenance/parse.go
Approach: Removed the local cosignBundle struct and its unmarshal in extractFromSig; replaced with cbundle.RekorBundle (github.com/sigstore/cosign/v2/pkg/cosign/bundle), same type already used by keyless.go's buildStaticOptions for the identical dev.sigstore.cosign/bundle annotation. title: refactor: break internal/enrichment <-> provenance import cycle
description:
internal/enrichment/provenance imports internal/enrichment (for enrichment.SubjectRef), so internal/enrichment cannot import the provenance package back. Two workarounds were added during ocidex-atd.13/.15 to route around this:

  1. internal/enrichment/provenance_drift.go declares provenanceFields — a hand-maintained partial copy of provenance.Provenance's JSON shape, with a comment asking future editors to keep the json tags in sync manually.
  2. adaptTrustResolver (service.TrustConfig -> provenance.TrustConfig) is copy-pasted verbatim into BOTH cmd/enrichment-worker/main.go and cmd/provenance-worker/main.go, ~18 lines each.

Neither workaround is load-bearing; both exist purely because a leaf data type lives in a non-leaf package.
design:
Move the shared data types down into a leaf package that neither side owns — e.g. internal/enrichment/types (or move SubjectRef itself, whichever produces the smaller diff):

  - SubjectRef, or
  - Provenance / RawArtifacts / TrustConfig

Then internal/enrichment can import the real Provenance type and provenanceFields is deleted outright. With TrustConfig in a leaf package, service.TrustConfig and provenance.TrustConfig can be unified into one type and both copies of adaptTrustResolver disappear.

Prefer moving the smaller surface. SubjectRef is one struct; the provenance types are three — but the provenance types are the ones actually causing duplication, so check both directions before committing.
acceptance_criteria: provenanceFields is deleted; recordProvenanceDrift unmarshals into the real provenance.Provenance type. adaptTrustResolver exists in zero or one place, not two. No new import cycle introduced (go build ./... passes). No behaviour change — existing dispatcher drift tests pass unchanged.
notes:
Files: internal/enrichment/subject/subject.go (new), internal/trust/trust.go (new), internal/enrichment/enrichment.go, internal/enrichment/provenance/{provenance,keyless,provenance_test,keyless_test}.go, internal/enrichment/provenance_drift.go, internal/service/registry.go, cmd/{enrichment,provenance}-worker/main.go
Approach: Extracted SubjectRef into leaf pkg internal/enrichment/subject (alias in enrichment.go preserves existing consumers) and TrustConfig into leaf pkg internal/trust (hard replace, zero external consumers). This let provenance_drift.go import the real provenance.Provenance type (deleted the hand-rolled provenanceFields mirror) and deleted the duplicated adaptTrustResolver bridge from both worker mains. go build/vet clean, all tests pass (incl. 6 TestDispatcher_ProvenanceDrift_* unchanged). golangci-lint has 64 pre-existing issues unrelated to this change (verified via git stash diff: identical count/category before and after).

title: No CI check for .tektonic source vs .tekton generated-YAML drift
description: Original premise is stale: 'make tekton-check' no longer exists (removed in 9e2d8d6); the Makefile only has tekton-synth. The specific drift cited is also resolved — .tektonic/shared.ts:11 is nodejs:24 and both helm specs are alpine/helm:4, matching .tekton/. notes:
Files: .tektonic/jobs/tekton-check/spec.ts, .tekton/tasks/tekton-check.k8s.yaml, CLAUDE.md
Approach: The drift guard already existed (e6965e4, gated on pipelineChanged in the PR pipeline) but could never fail. Two defects fixed:
(1) the nushell body used 'exit 1', which kills the process before tektonic's try/catch persists the code to /tekton/home/.exit-code; with onError:continue the task reported green on real drift. Now uses 'error make'.
(2) it used reportOnlyStatusReporter, so a correct failure still would not fail the PipelineRun. Now blocking (adds 'exit $exit_code' to report-status).
